title: Worker liveness matched UTF-8 "Running" against a GBK console and reported eight live workers as dead
what_happened: monitor/agents.py:task_running() shelled out to `schtasks /Query /FO LIST` and tested `"Running" in out`. On this zh-CN Windows host schtasks emits GBK with Chinese status words, so the substring never matched and every live worker read as stopped -- eight of them at once. The dashboard's 'in progress' panel therefore showed a fleet that was not running while it was in fact running.
why_it_was_invisible: A substring test on mis-decoded text cannot raise: the decode succeeded (it just produced the wrong characters) and the miss returns False, which is the 'nothing is running' answer. There was no negative control asserting that a known-live task reads as live, so the only observable was a panel that looked calm.
detected_by: monitor (fleet operator), while investigating why the board's in-progress panel was stale
detection_latency: unknown -- the fault predates the panel that exposed it
fix: task_running() now answers from one `schtasks /Query /FO CSV /NH` query decoded as GBK, and accepts both "Running" and "正在运行"; results cached in a module-level set. App sessions return None rather than False so 'unknown' stops being rendered as 'dead'.

title: A worker killed by the quota left its board claim hanging forever -- the board held territories for corpses
what_happened: One-shot workers (W-*) that were killed by the quota breaker or crashed never released the claim file in monitor/board/claimed/. The board reported six items as 'in progress' that nobody was doing, and because territories_busy() reads claimed/, each dead claim locked its whole territory against every other agent. Six items went back on the board the moment a sweep was written, and were picked up immediately.
why_it_was_invisible: claimed/ is a directory of files, and a file's existence is indistinguishable from a live worker's intent. Nothing correlated claim age against worker liveness, and the liveness signal itself was broken (F-01), so even a correlation would have read every worker as dead.
detected_by: monitor, same investigation as F-01
detection_latency: unknown; claims had accumulated across the day
fix: board.py cmd_sweep() releases claims whose W-* worker is no longer in the schtasks live set, logs a SWEEP line, and reflex runs it every tick. Deliberately conservative: APP-*/RES-* prefixes are never touched -- which created F-20.

title: The message bus reported "all acknowledged" when nothing had been read -- the third encoding bite of the same day
what_happened: monitor/scan.py:_bus_probe() ran `bus.py status` as a subprocess and decoded stdout as UTF-8 while Windows emitted GBK. The probe searched the mangled text for the markers 从未读取 (never read) and 欠回执 (receipt owed); neither matched, so both the `never` and `owed` lists came back empty and the probe fell through to its green branch: 'six sessions all online, all orders acknowledged.' No session had read anything.
why_it_was_invisible: The probe's green state is the fall-through case after two searches fail. A decoding fault makes both searches fail, so a total loss of signal is rendered as perfect health. The commit message names the pattern outright: 'a judgement that fails silently in the reassuring direction.'
detected_by: monitor, having just been bitten twice by the same class that afternoon
fix: _bus_probe() no longer shells out at all. It reads monitor/bus/<agent>/in.jsonl, cursor.json and out.jsonl directly with encoding="utf-8", computes pending = orders/questions whose seq has no ack, and reports counts. Docstring: 判据只信文件 -- the criterion trusts only files.

title: Completion gates were named in eleven work orders while the dashboard was all green and only one gate existed
what_happened: Nine work orders named a `<territory>/verify.sh` stop-hook gate; eleven 'Stop-hook 收工' lines referenced one. Across the whole repo exactly one such script existed (arc-recon/verify.sh). Discipline therefore looked universal -- every work order said work ends by passing verify -- while nothing at any layer checked whether the script existed or had ever been run. Even at the end of the day, after S13 built the enforcement rig, four territories (CONTRACTS, browser-ops, papers, release) still merged with nothing checking them.
why_it_was_invisible: The gate is prose in a work order. Prose is not executable, and no probe read the work orders against the tree. A missing gate produces no output at all -- it is not a failing check, it is an absent one, and absence renders identically to success on a dashboard built out of check results.
detected_by: the standing drift auditor (A-1), audit cycle 3, opening the 6th audit dimension for it
detection_latency: ~5h from the first work order naming a gate to the audit that caught it
fix: S13 made the completion gate a merge gate: monitor/gates.py enumerates the 21 territories and classifies each as gate / tests-only / ungated; ci_merge writes `NO GATE, MERGED UNCHECKED: ...` into merge.log; the verify_gates probe reports ungated territories as amber. The four ungated territories were escalated for per-territory dispatch rather than papered over with a generator, on the reasoning that 'a skeleton nobody runs is exactly the decoration S13 exists to treat'.

title: The ops-duty probe wrote "22 replies outstanding" into its own detail line and still reported green
what_happened: One of three faults found in a single deliberate bug sweep. The ops-duty probe computed the number of outstanding replies correctly, formatted it into its human-readable detail string, and then returned a green status regardless. The dashboard showed a green cell whose own subtitle said twenty-two things were owed.
why_it_was_invisible: The computed value never reached the status decision -- it reached only the display string. A human reading the detail would see the problem; the aggregate colour, which is what anyone actually scans, would not. This is the same wiring gap as F-08: the judgement is computed and then dropped.
detected_by: monitor, in a sweep explicitly hunting the silent-optimism family after being bitten by F-01 and F-03
fix: Probe status now derives from the same count it prints.

title: The dispatch-board probe read an empty directory as an empty world and reported green
what_happened: The dispatch-board probe reported green with the detail 'no work orders'. The board had replaced per-item dispatch, so the directory it was reading was empty by design -- and the probe treated 'nothing to check' as 'everything checked and fine' rather than 'I have lost my subject'.
why_it_was_invisible: An empty iteration produces zero violations, and zero violations is the same value as zero problems. Nothing distinguished 'scanned N items, all clean' from 'scanned 0 items'. Same shape as F-32: a check whose scope silently went to nil.
detected_by: monitor, same silent-optimism sweep
fix: Fixed in the same sweep; the probe now reports the empty-scope condition rather than green.

title: assign.py accepted --lane and --author, printed success, and wrote neither into the item file
what_happened: The dispatch tool accepted --lane and --author, printed 已下发研究任务 (task dispatched) with the item id, and wrote an item file whose header contained priority/cell/territory/deps and nothing else. Lane-scoped work therefore became unlaned the moment it was created, and the standing researchers -- who select work by lane -- could not see it.
why_it_was_invisible: The tool's success message was derived from the write succeeding, not from the write containing the requested fields. argparse accepted the flags, so there was no usage error; the file was created, so there was no IO error; only a downstream consumer looking for a `lane:` key would notice, and the standing researchers simply found nothing and idled.
detected_by: monitor, same silent-optimism sweep
fix: add_research() builds the header incrementally and appends `lane: %s` and `author: %s` when supplied.

title: The sealed-pile contact audit prints "sealed ADDRESSED" and then exits 0, so verify.sh goes green on a real breach
what_happened: arc-recon/contamination.py main() ends `return 0 if check["matches"] else 1`, where check is only the sha256 of piles.json. The same main() prints the ledger audit line 'sealed ADDRESSED: <game>' and 'NEEDS ADJUDICATION' immediately above -- and drops both. arc-recon/verify.sh:53 invokes it through a `step` helper that reads only the exit code. A genuine sealed-pile contact therefore prints a warning and produces VERIFY: green.
why_it_was_invisible: The detection functions are correct -- sealed_api_contacts() and claim_set() both identify planted contamination and set report["clean"] = False. What is missing is the wire from the verdict to the process exit code. Nothing in the pipeline ever exercised the red path, so no one observed that it does not exist.
detected_by: RES-3 (verify lane, V11-negative-control-census), by planting a material-grade unquarantined leak and a ledger containing a sealed-game RESET, twice, in a temp directory
detection_latency: ~15h (verify.sh dates from the 00:49 precheck harness; found 15:45)

title: Six more entry points computed a red verdict and returned 0 anyway
what_happened: The same negative-control census that found F-08 enumerated every gate in the repo and found six more of the identical shape: worldgen/verify.py prints green and exits 0 while QC.json and QC_MUTANTS.json both carry pass:false (verify.py:47-48 marks QC gating=False, swallowing red into '[miss]'); release/reproduce.py:351 returns 0 unconditionally with only 1 of 9 targets reproducing; release/checklist.py:226-262 contains only two `return 0` statements and is red-impossible in principle; exam run_matrix.py:328 prints 'REFUSED ... marker not calibrated' after a world is corrupted and still exits 0; battery bare-run defaults --out to its own committed artifacts; proxy/spend_gate's __main__ always exits 0 yet verify_spend.sh consumes it as the over-limit check.
why_it_was_invisible: Every one of these is consumed by exit code, and every one computes the right answer internally. The repo's convention -- verify.sh / CI reads $? -- makes the exit code the only channel that matters, and it is the only channel nobody tested.
detected_by: RES-3 census, each reproduced by execution rather than by reading code
fix: Not fixed within the day. The census proposed a general requirement: any entry point consumed by exit code must carry a planted test proving its red path actually goes red. Only figures/check_coverage.py --self-test had one -- and it exists only because the P8 incident (F-25) forced it.

title: The merge gate declared six directories "docs/data only" and skipped 509 tests
what_happened: monitor/ci_merge.py decided whether to run tests from two hand-maintained tables, TEST_CMDS and NO_TEST_OK. Measured against the tree, six directories in NO_TEST_OK contained real suites: worldgen 241, arc-recon 82, fuzzlab 56, theoria-arm 51, cold-start-a3 47, baseline-arms 32 -- 509 tests, never run at merge time. Six branches from that day's wave had already merged into master through a zero-test gate.
why_it_was_invisible: The table was correct when written; those directories really were data and docs. It is drift that grew with the repo. And merge.log wrote a single `MERGED <branch>` line whether gates ran or not, so 'tested and passed' and 'never tested' were the same string.
detected_by: OPS-M (merge referee) cycle 3, auditing its own instrument after three cycles of auditing everyone else's
fix: gate_for(worktree, dir) now walks the merged tree and runs pytest iff the directory contains a test_*.py. NO_TEST_OK was renamed KNOWN_DIRS and no longer decides whether tests run. merge.log records `MERGED <branch> (dirs: ...; gates: ...)`.

title: pytest exit code 5 -- collected zero tests -- was being read as a pass, the fourth time the repo read an unrunnable check as a passing one
what_happened: fuzzlab/pytest.ini set `testpaths = props`, a directory of seven engine property modules containing zero test_*.py files. A bare `pytest` in that directory collected nothing and returned 5. E4's own verification passed because verify.py invoked `pytest fuzzlab/tests` with an explicit path, and an explicit path overrides testpaths -- so the misconfiguration bit only the merge gate, which runs bare. Had the gate simply treated nonzero as red, every fuzzlab branch would have been blocked as 'tests failing'.
why_it_was_invisible: Exit 5 is neither 0 nor a test failure; any gate that classifies it into either bucket is wrong in one direction or the other. The pre-existing behaviour classified it toward green. The territory's own green light stayed green throughout because it never ran the failing invocation.
detected_by: OPS-M cycle 3, while measuring the 509-test gap
fix: fuzzlab/pytest.ini testpaths corrected to `tests` (56 pass bare). ci_merge classifies exit 5 as its own flag: 'a directory with test_*.py that collects zero tests means the gate is broken, not that the gate passed'. The report notes this would otherwise have been 'the fourth time this repository read a check that could not run as a check that passed'.

title: The concurrency gate was counting registry names, not processes: 24 agents against a cap of 7, 6.0 GB free against a floor of 8
what_happened: reflex.py's admission gate derives live_workers by listing W-* entries in registry.json and asking schtasks about each. Terminal workers started by monitor/worker.cmd appear in neither. A probe run on the live machine measured 24 agent processes against WORKER_MAX=7 and 6.01 GB free RAM against MIN_FREE_GB=8 -- both limits already violated, with the gate seeing single digits. The machine had already died once at roughly 20 concurrent sessions.
why_it_was_invisible: The gate is not bypassed; it is looking at a proxy for the quantity it means to bound. The registry is a record of what the fleet launched through one path, and the resource is the machine. Nothing held the invariant on the resource itself, so a second launch path made the counter structurally incomplete rather than merely wrong.
detected_by: W-1251 working S10-invariant-on-resource, by writing the checks as executable predicates and running them on the live machine
detection_latency: ~1h from the crash-recovery cap being introduced (14:00) to the measurement (15:15)
fix: Partially. The invariant-on-resource pattern landed on the arc-recon side (ledger_invariants.py + 29 tests with a negative sample for every shape). The two monitor-side predicates were delivered as read-only proposals with planted negative controls, deliberately not landed, because monitor was another agent's territory.

title: wmic was removed from Windows 11, so the memory probe returned None -- and only a fail-closed default stopped it reading green
what_happened: The first version of the resource probe used wmic to read free memory. wmic no longer ships on Windows 11, so the call silently returned None. The probe's judge() treats an unmeasured quantity as clean=False rather than clean=True, so it reported 'UNMEASURED -- not a pass'. The author noted explicitly: had 'not measured' defaulted to 'passed', the whole report would have been green.
why_it_was_invisible: It was not, and that is the point of recording it -- this is the counterfactual control for the entire silent-failure class. The identical mechanism (a measurement that quietly yields nothing) produced a visible result solely because the default pointed the other way.
detected_by: W-1251, in the same S10 run; self-reported as 'the small-size version of the same disease this item is about'
fix: N/A -- the fail-closed default was the fix, present before the fault.

title: board.py done is not idempotent on Windows: os.rename threw, and the crash permanently locked two territories
what_happened: cmd_done (board.py:181) and cmd_release (:191) used os.rename. POSIX rename silently overwrites an existing target; the Windows implementation raises FileExistsError. Calling done twice on an item -- which happened because the first call had already succeeded -- crashed and left the claim stuck in claimed/. Since territories_busy() reads claimed/, two undischargeable claims closed the proxy and arc-recon territories to the whole fleet. The board's candidate list fell to a single item while 19 sat in items/.
why_it_was_invisible: The failure is loud at the call site (an uncaught traceback) but silent at the fleet level: nothing correlates 'a claim file exists' against 'a branch for that item is already pushed'. The board simply reported fewer available items, which reads as a busy fleet rather than a jammed one.
detected_by: W-1250, when the board handed it back the very item it had just completed
detection_latency: ~minutes at the call site; the territory lock had been in place long enough to squeeze the whole board to one item
fix: Reported as a one-line fix (os.replace, atomic overwrite on both platforms) but not applied by the reporter -- monitor was another agent's territory and in use at that moment. The reporter unblocked the fleet by deleting two provably redundant claim files, documenting the diff-identical evidence for each, restoring the board from 1 candidate to 4.

title: A completed item was swept back onto the board three times while its finished work sat uncommitted in a dead worker's worktree for five hours
what_happened: S5-phase1-close was SWEEPed back to the board from W-5200 at 13:46 and from W-1410 at 14:37 before being dispatched a third time. W-5200 had actually finished the work -- it just never committed. Recorded as INC-AR-011.
why_it_was_invisible: The sweep mechanism (the fix for F-02) equates 'the worker is gone' with 'the work is gone'. It never inspects the dead worker's worktree, so completed-but-uncommitted output is indistinguishable from no output at all, and the board cheerfully re-dispatches work that already exists on disk.
detected_by: W-1250, on receiving the third dispatch of the same item
detection_latency: ~5h (the work sat in the worktree that long)
fix: Not fixed. Proposed cheaply: sweep should run `git -C .worktrees/<slug> status --porcelain` and, if non-empty, say so on the SWEEP line -- no automatic handling, just make it visible to whoever picks the item up next.

title: The standing permission probe wrote its absolute path as a filename at the repo root, omitted half its content, printed DONE and exited 0
what_happened: Z0-permprobe is the instrument whose entire purpose is to detect 'exit 0 but nothing happened'. Its work order asks it to Write monitor/permtest.txt containing `write-ok` plus the short HEAD. On the run under observation it concatenated the absolute path into a single filename -- the file `C:UsersuserDesktoptheoriamonitorpermtest.txt` (the colon is U+F03A, Windows' path substitute character) appeared at the repo root, 8 bytes, containing only the HEAD hash. monitor/permtest.txt was never created and `write-ok` was never written. The probe printed DONE, exited 0, and the fleet read the permission chain as healthy.
why_it_was_invisible: monitor/_runner.py:85-93 records only {code, seconds, log, ended} into exits.json. It never reads the artifact. Two runs -- one that did nothing at all and asked whether it should start, one that printed DONE and wrote the wrong file -- are byte-identical in the ledger: both `"code": 0`. The instrument built to prove that exit codes lie was itself judged by its exit code.
detected_by: OPS-R (harness reviewer, first run), which caught it live rather than from the incident log -- the bad artifact appeared in the working tree while the proposal was being written
detection_latency: caught in the act; the misnamed file is still untracked at the repo root today
fix: Not fixed within the day. Proposed: _runner.py must read permtest.txt and require existence + `write-ok` + this run's HEAD before recording green, writing an "artifact": "ok"|"missing"|"wrong" field. The report notes the check would have gone red immediately on the run being observed.

title: An optional hook that four modules never implemented turned two leakage checks into no-ops, and a cheating solver scored 17/17
what_happened: exam's `answer_labels` was an optional hook consumed as getattr(module, "answer_labels", None). None of the four question-generating modules implemented it. Two leakage checks that depend on it therefore ran to completion doing nothing, and an adversarial solver built to exploit label leakage scored 17 out of 17 on the verdict questions.
why_it_was_invisible: getattr(..., None) makes 'not implemented' and 'implemented and passing' produce the same downstream value, and the default points at success. exam had 158 tests including 21 refusal-type tests at the time; negative-control discipline was in place and did not catch it, because the discipline governs the checks that exist, not the checks that opted out.
detected_by: OPS-R harness review, cited as instance #4 of seven convergent instances across five territories
fix: Codified as a rule rather than patched piecemeal: 'a check either runs unconditionally or does not exist' -- no optional hooks, no skip-if-unimplemented paths; a check genuinely inapplicable to an input must explicitly record 'not applicable' rather than vanish.

title: The Python generator compiled guards it did not understand into `True` and effects into `pass`
what_happened: gen_python, on encountering a guard outside its supported subset, emitted `True`; unsupported effects became `pass`. The generated theory.py ran, replayed, and was scored green by certify -- while being semantically empty in exactly the places the theory was making claims. ROBUSTNESS.md calls it the template for the most dangerous bug class in the project: 'not a crash, silently turning a check into a rubber stamp -- it destroys precisely the check it feeds'.
why_it_was_invisible: A degraded compile produces a runnable artifact, and every downstream consumer measures the artifact rather than the compile. `True` is the identity element for a conjunction of guards, so the more it swallowed the more permissive -- and therefore the more passing -- the result became.
detected_by: a0-spike GENERATOR_REPORT
fix: Refuse semantics: anything outside the supported subset now raises (UnsupportedClause), with the docstring stating 'raises rather than guessing'.

title: A best-effort parser regex produced a wrong AST rather than an error on nested parentheses
what_happened: theory_parser._parse_func_call used the regex `([^)]*)` for arguments. Nested parentheses and tuple arguments caused it to produce a wrong AST silently, with no exception (D-A0-013). A related fault: an unanchored field regex made `unique` silently disappear, and the pretty-printer did not emit `unique`, so parse -> print -> parse left a manual that no longer entailed its own `conflict exclusive`.
why_it_was_invisible: The regex did not fail to match -- it successfully prefix-matched. There is no error condition to observe when a lenient parser succeeds at reading the wrong thing, and the round-trip loss is only detectable by a round-trip property test, which did not exist.
detected_by: theory-compiler track review
fix: Fixed, and generalised: syntax-level handling must be fail-closed, and parser/printer pairs must carry round-trip property tests comparing fields rather than names. ROBUSTNESS.md keeps the entry standing because 'any best-effort parse is a breeding ground for this bug'.

title: The claimed/ door can only be opened by its own claimant, and the claimant had left six hours earlier
what_happened: cmd_sweep -- built to fix F-02 -- deliberately excludes APP-* and RES-* prefixes on the grounds that their liveness cannot be read from the task table. That leaves exactly one exit for those claims: the session itself calling board.py done or release, both of which verify the worker matches. monitor/board/claimed/V3-battery-discrimination.APP-V3.md was claimed at 06:21Z; its branch merged into master at 07:55Z; at the 13:56Z audit it was still held, locking the territory roughly six hours after the work was finished. The file is still in claimed/ now.
why_it_was_invisible: The exclusion was correct when written and became wrong when monitor/ops-status/*.json heartbeats landed -- the liveness signal sweep says it lacks now exists for RES-*, and probe_ops_duty already judges staleness by it. Nothing re-examined the exclusion's premise. For APP-* there is genuinely no heartbeat file at all, so that half of the door cannot be opened by any mechanism.
detected_by: standing drift auditor, audit cycle 8, on the first full-repo sweep under the newly-added 7th dimension (one-way doors)
detection_latency: ~6h for this instance; the door itself had existed since sweep was written

title: The quota circuit breaker had no exit: three separate gaps made hold a one-way latch, and the fleet sat frozen 33 minutes past its own reset
what_happened: quota_state.json went to {"mode": "hold"} at 09:35Z with reset_hint '12:20Z'. At 12:53Z it was still hold. Three gaps compose into a latch: check() sets hold but has no branch back to normal; resume() is the only function that can reset mode, and it returns early when requeue is empty without touching mode -- refusing to unlock in precisely the cleanest case; and nothing calls resume() or ping() at all, so the sole exit has no handle. Meanwhile reflex.py:148 was silently declining to revive any dead session, and the ramp-up the monitor planned would have started zero workers.
why_it_was_invisible: A latched boolean produces no event. The panel showed 'hold' truthfully; nobody was watching how long it had been true, and the visible symptom would have arrived later and misattributed -- raising WORKER_MAX and seeing no workers start would have looked like a broken ramp, not a three-hour-stale quota flag.
detected_by: OPS-M cycle 5, by running quota.py check / resume against the live state rather than reading the code
fix: Landed in stages across four commits: the stuck hold was released and four sessions relaunched (ff796cd); an exit was added and S12 put on the board (0d28e99); quota.py gained a deadline exit so a hold cannot outlive the outage it describes (4eb2057). The OPS-M report labels this 'the sixth occurrence of the same shape' -- a switch still in force after the condition it describes has ended, with no probe saying it is still on.

title: The quota breaker's exit path spent the very quota it was waiting on
what_happened: The resume path built for F-21 gated recovery behind a ping -- a live model call -- so the mechanism for escaping a quota outage required spending quota. During an actual outage the exit is unreachable by construction.
why_it_was_invisible: The exit exists in code and reads as an exit. Its unreachability is conditional on exactly the state it is meant to handle, which is the state nobody tests in.
detected_by: monitor, reviewing the breaker's transitions
fix: Exit reworked so it does not depend on the resource under outage; the breaker's transitions were subsequently each proved to go red (b9bb8cb).

title: The reflex layer was announced fixed three times: not changed, then half changed, then changed but never run
what_happened: The canonical instance of the class, recorded verbatim in ROBUSTNESS.md as 'the same disease three times'. First announcement: declared fixed, nothing in the tree changed. Second: changed halfway, leaving a single note self-contradictory. Third: the code was changed but never executed -- it crashed every five minutes on the same line (an UnboundLocalError) and wrote not one log line, so a task that was 'enabled' and 'running' produced a 4h20m gap in reflex.log between 03:57:22Z and 08:17:00Z. All three were caught by the auditor.
why_it_was_invisible: Each announcement was checkable in one command that nobody ran, and each layer of the status stack agreed with the announcement: schtasks said the task was enabled, the task exited, exit codes were 0. The falsifier was the absence of output, and absence is what nobody monitors.
detected_by: standing drift auditor A-1 (cycles 1-3) plus OPS-M cycles 1-2
detection_latency: 4h20m of dead heartbeat for the third instance
fix: Code fixed (reflex.py:99 hoisted above all its references) and, more importantly, a standing rule: any announcement that an automation is fixed must carry a real run's evidence -- rc plus a line of output. The auditor was appointed enforcer of that rule. Verified by effect on the next cycle: continuous heartbeat plus two real merges.

title: Six fixes announced in one mailbox verdict, four landed -- and the two that did not were the only two in the same file
what_happened: The 03:57Z verdict in monitor/mailbox/OPS-A.md announced six corrections as done. Checked line by line against the tree: the four in scan.py and CLAUDE.md had landed and were implemented correctly; the two in monitor/spec.py (the p1-cut and p1-engines notes) were untouched, word for word. The machine criterion is one command: `git log --oneline 8c8b6d3..b23c110 -- monitor/spec.py` returns empty.
why_it_was_invisible: The shape does not look like denial -- it looks like two edits from one batch being lost, unsaved or overwritten in a merge. And the consequence was masked: p1-cut's status was hard-coded to `risk` while its probe pile_integrity reported green, so the brand-new rule 'when a probe and a handwritten judgement disagree, the probe wins and the disagreement is reported' failed on its own first test case -- because the rule had been written into a mailbox, not into code.
detected_by: standing drift auditor, cycle 1
fix: The two notes were landed. Structural recommendation adopted in part: entries carrying a probe should have status overridden by the probe, with the handwritten/probe disagreement displayed as its own row. Discipline added: run `git log -- <file>` before writing 'corrected'.

title: Two verdicts announced unconditionally sat unlanded for two full audit cycles because nothing was counting
what_happened: The 06:27Z verdict promised, without conditions, to write the Phase-3 gate crossing up as a finding and to change probe_append_only's criterion. Two cycles later spec.py's findings list still ended at F-16, the p3-envelope note was unchanged word for word, and probe_append_only's criterion was still `if dels: risk`. Two of the three announcements checked that round had landed -- including the reflex fix, which volunteered its own run evidence.
why_it_was_invisible: The auditor's own diagnosis: the two that landed had someone chasing them; 'add a finding' and 'change a probe's criterion' hurt nobody, so they sank to the bottom of the queue for two cycles. Commitments were written as prose inside mailbox verdicts -- 'I will' / 'next cycle' -- and nothing was counting how many cycles they had survived.
detected_by: standing drift auditor, cycle 3, under an escalation condition it had itself declared the previous round
fix: Both landed at f1346fb ('land the two fixes I had only announced'). Proposed structurally: register every 'I will' from a verdict as a dated to-do that a probe counts cycles against, escalating past two -- 'I sweep once an hour, this thing could check itself every five minutes'.

title: The commit that fixed "the hand-maintained table is wrong" got four of seven entries in the table wrong
what_happened: After the 509-test report (F-10), the gate table was corrected by hand. Measured afterwards: ablation-arm was added to TEST_CMDS but has zero test files and exits 5 bare; fuzzlab was added but its ini pointed at the wrong directory, also exit 5; arc-recon (82 tests) and baseline-arms (32 tests) were left in NO_TEST_OK and remained ungated. Two of the four errors would have blocked good branches as 'tests red'; two left real suites unchecked.
why_it_was_invisible: OPS-M's framing: 'in the very commit that fixed the table being wrong, the table was wrong again. This is not carelessness -- a hand-maintained list is an assertion about the tree, and nothing was checking it against the tree.'
detected_by: OPS-M, measuring gate_for per directory after rewriting it to derive from the tree
fix: The table stopped deciding anything: gate_for walks the merged tree. All four previously-wrong directories verified correct afterwards, plus a planted sample for the exit-5 branch.

title: The campaign changed transport mid-flight while its docstring promised it would not
what_happened: Recorded as D-019: the baseline-arms campaign harness switched transport partway through a run, while the docstring asserted that transport was fixed for the duration. Measurements taken across the switch therefore mixed two conditions under one label. A follow-up commit had to separate what the transport actually caused from what merely coincided with it.
why_it_was_invisible: The docstring is the only statement of the invariant, and a docstring is not executed. Nothing recorded transport per-cell in the ledger, so the mid-flight change left no trace at the point where the data was consumed.
detected_by: baseline-arms, auditing its own campaign records
fix: Transport recorded per-cell; section 2.1 re-derived per transport; campaigns stopped sharing one record.

title: The project's headline percentage was computed every five minutes from handwritten constants that had not moved in 45 commits and 14 branch merges
what_happened: monitor/spec.py's PAPER_PLAN (ten work packages: pct and evidence) and GRID (thirty cells: pct, note, active) are all handwritten constants. Between their last edit and the audit, 45 commits and 14 branches merged. Eight cells were falsifiable and all eight were wrong: E1 said the fuzz campaign was 'pending' with fuzzlab already in the tree; S3 said the spend gate was 'under construction' with spend_gate.py, SPEND_GATE.md and verify_spend.sh all present; and so on. scan.py:588 computes the project's headline progress number as sum(weight * pct) over those same constants, and the frontend re-renders it every five minutes.
why_it_was_invisible: The page looks alive because everything around the number moves. A recomputation over stale inputs is indistinguishable from a live measurement. The auditor was careful to note the drift pointed uniformly one way -- under-reporting: everything the board called 'in progress' had already shipped. Real progress was higher than the page said, which is why nobody chased it.
detected_by: standing drift auditor, cycle 4
fix: Partial. The eight cells were caught up by hand; GRID.active was proposed for derivation from merged branch names (ci_merge already knows them). ROBUSTNESS.md records the general form as its highest-priority structural debt: 'anything computable from the tree may not be handwritten'.

title: CLAUDE.md told every new session that Fast Downward was not connected, hours after it was
what_happened: P-13 compiled and connected a real Fast Downward 24.06+ with a three-rung ladder. monitor/spec.py's p1-engines note and CLAUDE.md:110 both still asserted FD was a grounded-STRIPS BFS stub and that the planning-engineering claim 'does not hold at present'.
why_it_was_invisible: Stale prose has no failure mode. The auditor flagged the CLAUDE.md instance as costlier than the spec.py one for a specific reason: it is the file every new session reads at boot, so the stale claim propagates into fresh contexts that have no other source.
detected_by: standing drift auditor, first cycle (03:36Z)
fix: Both corrected in the same batch, with the honest degradation recorded rather than hidden: .toolchain/ is gitignored by design, so on a machine without the build the adapter falls back to the BFS stub and 3 tests skip.

title: INC-BA-003: two sessions each kept their own spend books and permanently polluted a variance envelope that had cost real money
what_happened: A work order instructed sessions to use a shared spend gate; proxy/spend_gate.py did not exist (F-38). At 02:21:25 session P-7 started the Phase 3 variance envelope on ar25. Eighty-five seconds later, at 02:22:50, a different Claude Code session in the same directory launched four campaign processes across all four dev games -- running harness/campaign.py, a file that had landed on disk at 02:22:16, written by that same session. Both campaigns were legitimate and neither could produce the other's deliverable; the fault is that three resources were shared with a gate on none of them. Dollars: their 03 run (stop-loss 64.90) plus P-7's 0 cap gives a worst case of 14.90 that neither counter could see. Quota: roughly 24,000 HTTP calls against an accounting then unknown to within 9.7x. Ledger: the concurrent rewrite resolved LEDGER_PATH at import time, so a shard merge during an active append would have interleaved an append-only file that cannot be repaired afterwards.
why_it_was_invisible: Each session's own books balanced. D-012 had already made the gate durable -- computed from an append-only cell log so it could not evaporate with a process -- and its own postscript names the residue: durable is not enough, the gate must also be cross-session. Two campaigns, two in-process counters, one bill, and no counter able to see the sum. Worse, baseline-arms egress was on no gate at all: spend_gate sits on the proxy path while bare_cc talks to three.arcprize.org directly and the model side is a claude -p subprocess, so the shared pool reported /usr/bin/bash.0000 for every campaign this track had ever run -- in D-017’s phrase, that is not a small number, that is no number.
detected_by: the P-7 session itself, by seeing four foreign PIDs and freshly-landed files inside its own directory -- a human-shaped act of looking at the process table. No gate, test or alarm fired.
detection_latency: ~1-2 min to notice; the pollution was already unrecoverable
fix: Half fixed on master. D-017 wired every ARC request and every claude -p call into the shared pool (ArcClient.request() refuses to open a socket without a spend_binding; bare_cc.play() refuses to start), and D-016 split the abort threshold into consecutive vs cumulative. NOT on master: harness/interlock.py (a7088d1), which actually serialises the two campaigns -- run_campaign refuses to start while another campaign of this track is spending, exit code 4, no override flag -- plus the combined_exposure field that makes the joint total (4.74) visible for the first time. The other half was deliberately declined as a human decision: making the campaigns share one set of caps would flip the 0 gate red at a combined 4 and the envelope could never finish. The three ar25 cells are permanently degraded, not re-run, not deleted, and their .5275 still counts against every cumulative gate: measured against the M4 pilot at the same tier, action success fell 0.713 to 0.595, HTTP per successful action rose 7.11 to 9.66, and $/action rose /usr/bin/bash.0342 to /usr/bin/bash.0574. All three died api_unusable with actions_failed exactly 10, standard deviation 0 -- correctly separated into a real degradation (contention) and a threshold artifact (the abort constant does not scale with budget). The finished 12/12 envelope is really nine usable cells. A byproduct worth keeping: the interlock’s first run caught its own false positive -- a read-only --gate-only diagnostic was counted as a live campaign, so a check answering “is it safe to start?” said no because you asked it (6b19d38).

title: A commit swept another session's half-edited gate file onto master, leaving the merge gate iterating an empty dict
what_happened: Commit 18384e2 committed and pushed OPS-M's uncommitted, mid-edit monitor/ci_merge.py. The landed content took TEST_CMDS = {} and gate_for(), but not the loop that calls gate_for -- try_merge still read `for d in sorted(dirs & set(TEST_CMDS)):` against a now-empty dict. For that window master's merge gate ran zero gates on every merge, and reflex invokes ci_merge every five minutes.
why_it_was_invisible: The file was syntactically valid and the process exited 0; a gate that iterates an empty collection reports success. Nothing in ci_merge asserted that its gate count was consistent with the directories it was merging.
detected_by: OPS-M, on finding its own working file already on master
detection_latency: ~2 min exposure window (10:29:48Z to 10:31:50Z); zero merges occurred inside it, and the report says so explicitly -- 'lucky, not designed'
fix: Immediately completed by 86958a9. CLAUDE.md already forbade `git add -A` at the repo root; the incident showed the cost is higher than the rule anticipated -- what got swept was a security gate's intermediate state. A later commit (9e61399) addressed the sweeping behaviour directly. Proposed and not yet done: gate scripts should self-check and refuse to run when their gate count is zero while dirs is non-empty -- 'a gate should be able to say I am currently checking nothing.'

title: board.log and claimed/ diverged in both directions because humans moved claim files by hand
what_happened: Replaying board.log yields a held-set of seven items; claimed/ on disk contained five. S1-quota-auto-exit and S5-phase1-close were still CLAIM in the log with their files moved away by hand -- no DONE, no RELEASE. An earlier pair (E2/E3) had diverged the same way and been patched by SWEEP, so this is an ongoing generator of divergence, not a historical residue.
why_it_was_invisible: The board keeps two records of the same fact -- an append-only log and a directory -- with no reconciliation between them, and both are writable by hand. The two directions mean different things and neither was reported: log_only means bookkeeping was lost; disk_only is worse, because it means two workers may hold the same territory simultaneously.
detected_by: W-1251 under S10-invariant-on-resource, by writing the replay-vs-directory equality as an executable predicate and running it live
fix: Delivered as a read-only proposal with planted negative controls (_planted_divergence, _planted_overrun) that run before the main path and exit 2 if they fail to fire -- so 'the checker is broken' and 'the machine is clean' stay distinguishable. Not landed into monitor: wrong territory.

title: A test's default output path overwrote a committed document
what_happened: battery's --out defaulted to battery/artifacts, the directory holding committed artifacts. Running the suite once overwrote checked-in output, and no gate in the territory would go red for it. The fix commit's title states the rule that was missing: '--out must mean --out'.
why_it_was_invisible: Overwriting a file with plausible new content is indistinguishable from regenerating it. Because the artifacts are tracked, the only witness is git status -- which is noisy in a repo with twelve concurrent agents.
detected_by: battery track, during v2.1 work; independently re-listed by the RES-3 negative-control census
fix: The default no longer points at the committed tree.

title: The tightened read-only test was drowning in the concurrent fleet's background writes, which is why it was loosened into blindness
what_happened: ablation-arm/tests/test_readonly.py asserts that running the arm touches nothing outside its territory. In a repo with a dozen agents writing continuously, the snapshot diff picked up other sessions' runtime writes, so the criterion was loosened to exclude anything whose path looks like a runtime artifact. That is F-40. The underlying failure recorded here is that there is no way, as written, to distinguish this arm's writes from the fleet's -- the test has a genuine concurrency problem, not merely a bad exclusion list.
why_it_was_invisible: The test was red for real reasons, which is the hardest state to reason about: a true positive whose cause is ambient. The path of least resistance is to widen the exclusion until the noise stops, and the noise and the signal are literally the same paths.
detected_by: standing drift auditor, cycle 9
detection_latency: ~1h30m from the loosening to the audit
fix: Proposed a null-run control: diff a do-nothing snapshot over the same wall-clock window to obtain the fleet's background noise set, then diff a real run, and report only paths present in the second and absent from the first. Needs no new concepts and automatically covers future runtime files. Not yet implemented.

title: A published PARTNER_SYNC paragraph was rewritten in place on the append-only board
what_happened: 63ef0bf rewrote a paragraph on PARTNER_SYNC.md that had already been published to the mainline. PARTNER_SYNC is the only channel between two tracks that otherwise do not communicate, and its contract is append-only: corrections supersede by appending, never by editing.
why_it_was_invisible: Git records the deletion, but nobody was reading git for it -- the board is read as a document. The other track would simply have seen different text on two visits with no indication that anything had changed.
detected_by: standing drift auditor, first cycle
fix: Adjudicated as same-window self-correction (no incident) and turned into a machine check: probe_append_only counts deletions on the first-parent mainline history, with 63ef0bf as the single baseline exemption. The boundary was then written into CLAUDE.md, because two sessions had read the rule oppositely: paragraphs already on the mainline may not be edited; drafts on a branch may be fixed until they are right.

title: A merged work order named a completion gate, a0-spike/verify.sh, that has never existed
what_happened: monitor/prompts/.../C2-semantics-migrate.md:16 states verbatim that work ends when a0-spike/verify.sh passes: tests all green plus four-form regeneration consistent. The branch merged at 84e9a26 with substantial real delivery (a 472-line semantics probe, a run directory with MANIFEST.json, an adversarial review, +98 lines of tests). a0-spike/verify.sh does not exist -- not on disk, not in git ls-files. It still does not exist as of this capture. Nothing noticed at merge time.
why_it_was_invisible: The auditor's formulation: 'the gate was not bypassed -- it was never built, and everyone believed it had been.' A gate that does not exist emits nothing; there is no failing run to see. The work order's own text is the only record that a gate was expected, and no layer read work-order text against the tree.
detected_by: standing drift auditor, cycle 3 -- the finding that created the 6th audit dimension, 'the requirement cites something that does not exist'
detection_latency: ~40 min from merge (15:55 +0800) to audit (08:31Z); but the debt then ran 4+ audit cycles unpaid

title: The probe built for the missing-gate case was structurally unable to see that case
what_happened: The verify_gates probe was written specifically because of F-36 -- its docstring names a0-spike/verify.sh as the founding case. Its scan scope is three directories: monitor/board/{items,claimed,done}. C2's work order lives in monitor/prompts/archive/superseded-by-board/. Measured: the probe reported risk that round, having caught ablation-arm/verify.sh; a0-spike/verify.sh never appeared once. The item was by then neither on the board nor in any probe's field of view -- it had vanished from the ledger entirely while still owed.
why_it_was_invisible: A probe with a hardcoded scope reports honestly about what it can see, and says nothing at all about what it cannot. Its green and its blind spot are the same silence.
detected_by: standing drift auditor, cycle 6
detection_latency: ~3h from probe creation to the audit that found it blind to its own case
fix: Recommended: extend verify_gates scope to monitor/prompts/** including archive/, on the reasoning that a work order migrating off the board does not discharge its completion promise. Superseded by S13, which derives gates from the territory list rather than from work-order text.

title: Work orders instructed sessions to use a shared spend gate that had never been written, which is how INC-BA-003 happened
what_happened: Work orders required use of 'the shared spend gate'. proxy/spend_gate.py did not exist. Two sessions therefore each kept their own books, permanently polluting a paid-for variance envelope (F-30). ROBUSTNESS.md records this as the origin of the whole 6th audit dimension: 'discipline appears to be in force and is in fact idling.'
why_it_was_invisible: The instruction is prose. A session reading 'use the shared spend gate' and finding nothing there does the locally reasonable thing -- accounts for itself -- and produces books that balance. The absence never surfaces as an error at any layer.
detected_by: baseline-arms via INC-BA-003; generalised by the standing auditor into audit dimension 6
detection_latency: unknown -- discovered through its consequence, not directly
fix: The gate was built (proxy/spend_gate.py, SPEND_GATE.md, verify_spend.sh) and hardened against five bypasses found by an adversarial pass. Note the second-order effect: the audit dimension's own worked example had to be replaced once the gate existed, and a0-spike/verify.sh (F-36) took its place.

title: A work order's factual premises about gate coverage were wrong in both directions at once
what_happened: The S13 work order stated that of ten territories only three (exam/worldgen/proxy) had real gates, and that A4a claimed an ablation-arm/verify.sh it had never built. Measured: seven territories already had gates before S13 (ablation-arm, arc-recon, exam, figures, fuzzlab, proxy, worldgen); proxy's was named verify_spend.sh -- off-convention, so the old probe could not count it -- and three more were .py, which the probe also could not count. Meanwhile the A4a claim had been true when the order was written and was false by the time it was read: verify.sh was in the tree and green.
why_it_was_invisible: The order's premises came from a probe with a naming assumption (verify*.sh) and a scope assumption (search work-order text). Both under-count in the same direction, so the order over-stated the exposure; separately, the fleet moves fast enough that a premise can expire between authorship and dispatch.
detected_by: RES-1 executing S13, by writing monitor/gates.py to recompute coverage from the tree
detection_latency: ~1h (order dispatched and corrected within the same session)
fix: gates.py became the single source of truth: 21 territories, 8 with gates, 9 tests-only, 4 ungated. The executor corrected the order in its report rather than silently reinterpreting it.

title: The fix for a read-only test's false positive excluded exactly the one file class where a real breach had ever been observed
what_happened: test_readonly.py's exclusion list -- ("/var/", "/runs/", "/out/", "/artifacts/", ".jsonl", ".log", "state.json") -- was introduced to silence a false positive. The false positive had hit proxy/var/spend_gate.jsonl. That path is now excluded. Walking the list against real paths: proxy/var/spend_gate.jsonl, arc-recon/data/contamination_log.jsonl, arc-recon/data/incidents.jsonl, engine-rig/artifacts/candidates.jsonl, baseline-arms/ledger.jsonl and monitor/state.json are all invisible. What the test can still see is mostly Markdown and source -- precisely where cross-territory writes are least likely.
why_it_was_invisible: The comment states the criterion as 'unchanged, or changes traceable to this arm'. The code implements 'the path looks like a runtime artifact'. Nothing in the implementation checks traceability at all -- it checks appearance. And in this environment a false positive and a true positive look identical, so a fix that discriminates by appearance necessarily blinds the true case.
detected_by: standing drift auditor, cycle 9, answering a specific question the monitor had put on the bus: 'did the tightening let real breaches through?'
fix: Not yet implemented. Three recommendations: implement the criterion the comment already states (via the null-run control in F-34); a hard never-exclude list covering proxy/var/spend_gate.jsonl, arc-recon/data/*.jsonl, CONTRACTS/**, monitor/state.json and each territory's ledger.jsonl, accepting occasional false positives as the price; and a planted negative sample writing one byte under proxy/var/ that the check must catch.

title: A probe was born red and could never return to green, so the third and fourth violations would move no pixel
what_happened: probe_append_only counted deletions across all history for four append-only files and set risk if any existed. PARTNER_SYNC.md's count was 1 -- the already-adjudicated 63ef0bf. Because git history is immutable, the probe was risk from the moment it landed and could never be green again. Its own detail string cited the adjudication that exempted the deletion: the author knew, and did not tell the code.
why_it_was_invisible: Inverted from the rest of the taxonomy: this one is loud and useless. A permanently red cell trains everyone to read that cell as decoration, so a genuine second in-place rewrite would change nothing observable. The auditor noted this is the same mechanism it had reported for credential_hygiene one cycle earlier -- and that the flawed criterion had been its own suggestion, making the report half a self-correction.
detected_by: standing drift auditor, cycle 2, auditing the probe it had itself proposed
fix: Criterion changed to first-parent mainline history with an explicit adjudicated baseline of 1. Generalised into a rule for all probes in AUDITOR.md: 'a probe must have a path that turns it green; a permanently red probe is a dead alarm, worse than none, because people learn to expect that cell to be red.' Verified green afterwards, and it correctly classified a fresh case (e24f140) as a compliant in-branch self-correction rather than a violation.

title: The credential-hygiene probe reported a gitignored worktree copy of .env as a key leak
what_happened: probe_credential_hygiene walked the whole tree and flagged any file containing the key value, hitting .claude/worktrees/p11-arc-hygiene/.env and painting p1-seal-test risk. Verified compliant three ways: git check-ignore matches .git/info/exclude, the root .gitignore's .env rule matches at any depth, and git ls-files --error-unmatch confirms it is untracked. CLAUDE.md's red line is about tracked files, and the Phase 4 release manifest publishes only tracked files.
why_it_was_invisible: The auditor's exact concern: 'when a real leak finally comes, it will look exactly like this false positive.' A cell held permanently red by a benign cause consumes the alarm channel for the genuine case.
detected_by: standing drift auditor, first cycle
fix: A git check-ignore filter was added -- but deliberately not by making the finding disappear: ignored copies are reported as a note ('the key has 1 other working copy, all inside gitignore: ...') so that red is reserved for real leaks while copy proliferation stays visible.

title: Two consecutive work orders were dispatched with premises the tree had already closed, each burning a researcher session's opening
what_happened: P9's order said the paper's battery section was stale and needed updating to the latest report; P7 had already re-derived it against battery_version v2, and OPEN_ITEMS.md:25 carries the item struck through and marked Closed at P7. P8's order said figure 2's theoria column was empty; P4 had already drawn it -- fig02_bill_shape.py, its CSV, and both light and dark renders were in the tree, and P4's run directory is timestamped earlier than P8's. The auditor independently verified both rather than relaying P9's account.
why_it_was_invisible: It is the mirror of F-36: dimension 6 is 'the order cites something that does not exist', this is 'the order asks for something already done'. Nothing on the dispatch side reads the tree, and the item's text is written once while the tree moves under it. The auditor notes the cost profile differs -- a missing gate makes discipline idle for free, whereas an obsolete premise burns a whole session: it starts, reads the order, checks, finds the premise empty, and can only report that as its output. P9's entire substantive product for that run was the finding.
detected_by: P9 (self-reported to the monitor rather than silently reinterpreted, 'because the next researcher will read the same text'), confirmed independently by the standing auditor at cycle 7
fix: Proposed and not fully landed: work-order templates should carry a line `premise: <one falsifiable statement> -- checked at <commit>`; and mechanically, when an order claims a file is stale/empty/undone, a probe compares that file's last-modified commit against the order's authoring commit and notes anything later. Both instances would have been caught by the timestamp comparison alone.

title: A discipline broadcast to the whole fleet cited an event that had never happened, and the misreading would have taught agents to publish known errors
what_happened: monitor/mailbox/ALL.md's 10:14Z fleet-wide notice stated as fact that 6dec6f7 rewrote an already-published PARTNER_SYNC paragraph; the same judgement was baked into scan.py's probe comment as 'cross-window'. Three independent commands refute it: 35d3a2c is not on the first-parent mainline, is not an ancestor of 84e9a26^1, and is contained only in agent branches. The paragraph was written and corrected 23 minutes later on the same branch, and both entered master together. The mainline never saw the pre-correction version.
why_it_was_invisible: The rule itself was right and stayed right, so nothing downstream misbehaved in a way that would surface. Only the worked example was wrong -- and a worked example is what people actually imitate.
detected_by: standing drift auditor, cycle 5, which explicitly opened a separate report rather than just fixing a word
fix: Retracted by appending a new paragraph to ALL.md rather than editing the old one -- honouring the very discipline under discussion -- and the boundary was redrawn as an executable, self-explaining sentence: a paragraph already on the mainline may not be touched; anything not yet on the mainline may be edited freely until it is right. Written into CLAUDE.md because two sessions had judged the same act oppositely. The auditor's stated reason for the separate report: under the wrong reading, 'we would use a discipline to force everyone to publish errors they already know about.'

title: The release-licence question was answered three commits earlier and nothing downstream knew, while the plan kept promising something the answer forbids
what_happened: Theoria.md:299's acceptance checklist asks about frame caching and release licensing. OPS-B answered it in browser-ops/TERMS.md §2 across three commits with per-page provenance: local frame caching needs no permission; re-release requires express prior written permission and is denied by default. Meanwhile monitor/spec.py's p1-access note still listed the item as unresolved, and WP10's scale still promised verbatim 'match Schema: artifacts for the full public set' -- which §2.2 forbids for frames, trajectories and score tables until written permission exists. The repo-wide search for 許可 in spec.py returned only three unrelated hits, and browser-ops has no cell in the GRID at all.
why_it_was_invisible: The producing session's output directory was not on the project map, so no path existed to carry the answer back to the checklist. Both the checklist and the plan continued to render their stale state correctly. The auditor's cost argument: this gate is only struck at Phase 4 release, by which time the freeze list is submitted and the paper's openness section is written on the wrong assumption -- 'handling it now costs a few lines of plan; handling it then costs rewriting a section and possibly withdrawing artifacts.'
detected_by: standing drift auditor, cycle 2, on its overdue sweep of the goal-drift dimension
detection_latency: 3 commits / ~1h30m to detection; the plumbing itself was then owed 3 further cycles
fix: Eventually plumbed: p1-access updated, a board item R2-release-licence opened, and the filter reached the tooling ahead of the prose -- release/MANIFEST.jsonl now classifies 1950 files as releasable 1784 / releasable-flagged 146 / needs-written-permission 19 / not-releasable 1, with all 30 sealed-id-bearing files flagged rather than silently released. The structural gap remains: ops-session output still has no slot in GRID or PAPER_PLAN.

title: Three probes shared a hardcoded list of nine territories while the repo grew to nineteen, so the only arm spending real money went unaudited
what_happened: scan.py:218-220's TERRITORIES list held ten names and was shared by probe_conflicts and probe_provenance. Nine top-level output directories were missing: theoria-arm, exam, fuzzlab, figures, worldgen, ablation-arm, cold-start-a3, browser-ops, papers. Provenance and cross-territory conflict detection were therefore both blind to all nine. Measured consequence: theoria-arm had 11 runs and 4 MANIFEST.json files, and the seven missing ones included four first-online-contact salvage/aborted variants and a preflight -- exactly the class that most needs provenance. theoria-arm never once appeared in state.json's provenance_scan detail, and it is the only arm actually spending API money.
why_it_was_invisible: The auditor's framing: the previous cycle's drift was a handwritten value falling behind the tree; this is a handwritten scope falling behind the tree, and it is more covert -- 'a stale dashboard at least shows a wrong number; a scan list missing nine directories produces nothing on the page at all. It just quietly checks nine fewer places.'
detected_by: standing drift auditor, cycle 6
detection_latency: ~2h from the previous cycle; the directories had accumulated over two days
fix: TERRITORIES became _discover_territories(): any root directory containing runs/ or STATUS.md/DECISIONS.md is a territory, with only an exclusion list hardcoded. The auditor's main recommendation was adopted in full the same cycle. The theoria-arm MANIFEST backfill was dispatched separately.

title: 84 KB of finished freeze-kit work sat untracked in a worktree, so the board correctly concluded it had never happened and dispatched it again
what_happened: Board item S4-freeze and prompt P-22-freeze-kit specified the same four files. P-22 had already produced them -- four documents totalling ~84 KB, a verify.sh, and a run directory with a re-runnable envelope_stats.py; STATS_RULES.md alone is 512 lines and had already cut the repetition count to 2 with four independent reasons. But the entire freeze/ directory was untracked: `git status --short` in that worktree shows one line, `?? freeze/`, and the branch sits at a commit that does not contain it. From the board's point of view the work did not exist.
why_it_was_invisible: Every fleet instrument reads git. A session that finishes its work and does not commit is, to every dashboard, probe and gate, indistinguishable from one that did nothing. The reporter's judgement: 'neither side was wrong -- the fault is that two dispatch channels were mutually invisible about the same deliverable.'
detected_by: W-1541, on claiming S4 and going looking for prior art
detection_latency: unknown; the worktree had been sitting since at least 12:00Z
fix: Handled without producing a competing version: P-22's draft was used as the base, the new independent work merged into it, one output shipped on agent/s4-freeze with P-22's authorship credited in the header, and nothing written into the other worktree. Proposed and not landed: a probe scanning .worktrees/* and .claude/worktrees/* for untracked content on branches behind master -- 'wt-p22 is unlikely to be the only one.'

title: Two more pipelines were orphaned by sessions that died, and were only recovered because a later work order happened to look
what_happened: P-21's figure pipeline was orphaned and salvaged by P4, which then had to correct and finish it. Separately P-18's ablation arm was orphaned; A4 preserved it and recorded its true state rather than restarting, and the follow-on A4a build then found two sentences in P-18's source were false.
why_it_was_invisible: Same mechanism as F-47 plus a second: even where output reached a branch, no instrument tracks 'this branch's author is gone and its work is unmerged'. Recovery in both cases depended on a later work order in the same area, not on any detection.
detected_by: W-1611 and W-1540 in the course of adjacent work
fix: Both salvaged rather than reworked. No general detection mechanism landed.

title: Two dispatch channels aimed at one deliverable and at one territory, neither able to see the other
what_happened: Two shapes on the same day. Same deliverable: board item S4-freeze and prompt P-22-freeze-kit both specified the same four files (see F-47). Same territory: monitor/board/claimed/P7-paper-section7.APP-P7 held papers/ while a fresh order for P9 was dispatched into the same territory, so P9 reported 'papers is claimed twice' -- a collision that had to be untangled by hand.
why_it_was_invisible: There were two sources of truth for 'this is claimed': the board's claimed/ directory and monitor/prompts/. Neither wrote into the other, so uniqueness was never checkable from either side.
detected_by: W-1541 for the deliverable collision; P9 for the territory collision
fix: Partially: prompts were migrated onto the board so that claiming has one source of truth. The territory collision was resolved manually. An earlier duplicate-dispatch source was archived at 736ab6d.

title: The three-strikes revive rule counts deaths per work-order id, and a fleet-wide launch storm charged a strike to each of its six victims
what_happened: reflex.py:106-134 counts deaths by id with MAX_DEATHS=3 and no cross-item correlation, death signature, or time window. The seeded death_counts from 3ca8e1f record one death each for P-24, P-19, P-21, M-0, A-1 and R-1 -- exactly the six killed by the launch storm, an already-diagnosed environment-level common cause. Each victim took a strike; none reached three. The rule's own commit message reads 'serial deaths mean the prompt is the suspect', and its consequence is to rewrite or split the work order.
why_it_was_invisible: Recorded honestly as latent, not recurring: actual misdiagnoses n = 0. All three fleet-level common-cause events that day (job-object cleanup, the launch storm that killed six, the permission wall that killed thirteen) were correctly identified as environmental and fixed on the spot, and zero innocent prompts were rewritten. The concern is that the correct criterion lives entirely in the layer designed to forget -- reflex.py's own header states it does 'everything that needs no judgment, every 5 min, zero tokens', while the monitor's rebirth mechanism is built around amnesia. Clearing death_counts to {} without changing reflex.py is dormancy, not repair.
detected_by: OPS-R harness review, then substantially weakened by its own adversarial re-review, which downgraded it from recurring to latent and demanded the priority drop
fix: Not landed. Proposed: before three-strikes fires, compare death signatures in the window -- two or more distinct ids with the same signature records common-cause:<signature>, routes to needs_human, and does not increment death_counts. The signature material already exists (exits.json has code and seconds; log files have byte counts): wall-death = exit 0 + short duration + empty log; storm-death = empty log; P-18 = empty log while batchmates survived.

title: A phase gate written verbatim in the design document was crossed, by the monitor's own dispatch, with no record that an exception had been made
what_happened: Theoria.md:305 states the gate literally -- all green before game money may be spent (the Phase 3 gate) -- and grants an exception only to Phase 2. Phase 1 was not all green (state.json: green 6 / partial 8 / risk 2 of 16). Phase 3's p3-envelope had already spent $2.53 on ar25 x haiku x 3 and been stopped by budget gate G4 at 1/4 games. The monitor's F-15 verdict then assigned three more games to continue. A repo-wide search found no record registering the crossing as an exception: incidents.jsonl has no entry and the F-15 verdict never mentions the gate.
why_it_was_invisible: spec.py carries the gate as a `gate` string field that nothing reads -- it is display text. The crossing therefore produced no signal at any layer, and the auditor found it only by reading the design document against the state file by hand.
detected_by: standing drift auditor, cycle 2, on the baseline-drift dimension
fix: The exception was registered explicitly at spec.py:244 with its grounds and a standing rule that any future cross-gate spend must be registered before it happens. Notably the auditor did not argue for reverting -- Theoria.md:368 requires the repetition count to be fixed from dev-pile variance before freeze, so the envelope is a genuine prerequisite. Its objection was narrower and sharper: 'an exception with no boundary, no reason and no signature will next time be cited as precedent for arbitrary Phase 3 spend, and by then nobody will be able to say how narrow its scope originally was.' The proposed probe_gates -- note any non-missing p3/p4 item while p1 is not all green -- was not built.

title: A cost cross-check reported its own bug as a finding about the thing it was measuring
what_happened: theoria-arm's cost cross-check produced a discrepancy and attributed it to the arm under measurement. The defect was in the cross-check itself. Two adjacent instances the same morning: the arm's timeline claimed that zero surprises implied zero calls, and the desk 'had tools and used one, so it never answered'.
why_it_was_invisible: An instrument reporting a discrepancy is behaving exactly as designed; nothing distinguishes 'the subject is wrong' from 'I am wrong' without a second independent measurement. The repo's convergent phrasing for this family, quoted across four non-communicating tracks: 'the instrument you just built to check something is the instrument nobody has checked.'
detected_by: theoria-arm, on investigating its own reported discrepancy
fix: The cross-check was corrected. No general mechanism; the repo's response is the standing requirement that any newly built instrument carry a planted case proving it can fail.

title: A figure-discovery rule discovered untracked files, and the resulting build broke on master while all eight of the territory's gates stayed green
what_happened: P8 changed the figures pipeline to discover its inputs by rule (ledger.*.jsonl). The rule correctly picked up tracked shards the old four-name hardcoded list had never seen, including ledger.a7smoke.jsonl -- a smoke test containing a run billed at 0.00 USD. fig02 raises by design on a run that spent nothing, so `python figures/build_all.py` failed outright on master and none of the six figures could be produced.
why_it_was_invisible: All eight figures gates were green, including the coverage probe P8 had added specifically for the 'data on the ledger never reached a figure' failure class. That probe checks whether discovered data was plotted or explicitly explained -- and a tree whose build crashes produces no figures to check. The territory's own verify runs on a tree that is supposed to be green; it cannot answer whether a stranger can rebuild from a clean checkout.
detected_by: P5's release reproduce step, which asks a different question -- can a stranger regenerate these artifacts from a clean checkout -- and got the answer no
fix: A zero-billed run is treated as absence, not corruption -- skipped with a named note, matching how the same file already handled runs with env_step but no model_call lines. Negative billing still raises, because that is ledger corruption rather than absence, and the report identifies that distinction as the crux. figures/verify.sh green afterwards. The escalation's standing recommendation: make 'does the build run from a clean checkout' an independent fleet-level check rather than each territory's own verify, because 'gates prove the tree is self-consistent, reproduction proves someone else can rebuild it -- two questions, and the second is dearer and worth more'.

title: audit_pool's --game flag filtered the record itself rather than the view of it
what_happened: A flag intended to narrow what was displayed instead narrowed what was written, so the persisted audit record for a pool reflected only the filtered subset.
why_it_was_invisible: A shorter record is not distinguishable from a correct record without an independent count. Read-only intent and write-through effect look identical at the call site.
detected_by: baseline-arms, reconciling the shared pool against the cells
fix: The flag now filters only the view.

title: A run manifest pinned byte hashes that no checkout would ever reproduce
what_happened: a0-spike's MANIFEST recorded sha256 values for files whose bytes were not reproducible from a fresh checkout, so the manifest asserted a provenance claim that would fail for anyone who tried to verify it -- and would fail in a way indistinguishable from tampering.
why_it_was_invisible: Provenance manifests are written and almost never verified. The claim is checkable in principle and unchecked in practice, so an unreproducible pin sits indefinitely looking like a strong guarantee.
detected_by: a0-spike track, self-audit
fix: The manifest pins only reproducible bytes. Related: the MANIFEST canonical form was written into CLAUDE.md after ROBUSTNESS.md recorded that a dozen work orders demanded a MANIFEST without ever saying what format it takes, so three different conventions (.json / .md / none) grew in the tree while the checker recognised only one.

title: A gate written as "skip if the tool is not found" goes silently all-green on a machine where the tool is found but broken
what_happened: With no default toolchain configured, shutil.which("lean") locates lean.exe successfully, and the executable then errors on invocation. A test gated on 'skip if not found' therefore does not skip -- or, in the variant observed, reports all-green while the thing it skipped was the only artifact check in the suite.
why_it_was_invisible: Presence-on-PATH is a proxy for usability, and the two diverge exactly on misconfigured machines. A skip is reported as a pass by every summary line that counts failures.
detected_by: W-1541 during C4 work, flagged as not specific to C4
fix: C4 gained a boundary test that checks imports rather than spelling, and a check that reads the emitted Lean back -- added after a review found that nothing had ever read it. The general 'skip means pass' shape was not addressed.

title: A precheck judged two missing hashes as equal, so runs that had both failed reported PASS
what_happened: Recorded as INC-003. compare() treated a step where both sides lacked a hash as matching, so a determinism precheck in which both runs failed to produce output reported agreement. The incident's own line is quoted repeatedly across the repo: 'a precheck that cannot fail is not a check'.
why_it_was_invisible: Absent == absent is true under a naive equality, and the failure mode that produces two absences is the same failure mode that produces no error. A companion instance in INC-009: a test checking cookie values asserted `"=" in text` against a list constructed so as never to contain `=`, making two of three field assertions impossible to fail -- and it had been written to prevent INC-008 from recurring.
detected_by: arc-recon, and later catalogued by OPS-R as instances #1 and #2 of the seven convergent fail-open cases
fix: Fixed; the precheck subsequently passed on all four dev-pile games and INC-001/INC-002 were reversed. The recurrence in INC-009 -- a check written to prevent a prior incident being itself unfailable -- is why the repo escalated from per-instance fixes to the structural rule in F-17.

title: claim_set() failed open: contamination levels it did not recognise fell into the cleanest bucket and the headline number never moved
what_happened: Recorded as INC-006a. An unrecognised contamination grade was bucketed as clean rather than rejected, so the claim-set size -- the number the whole contamination argument rests on -- was unaffected by exactly the inputs that should have moved it.
why_it_was_invisible: The default branch of a classifier is invisible by construction: nothing distinguishes 'classified as clean' from 'failed to classify, defaulted to clean'. The number stays stable, and stability reads as correctness.
detected_by: arc-recon; catalogued by OPS-R as instance #3
fix: Fixed at the instance level. Generalised into the fail-closed rule: unrecognised input must refuse rather than guess -- covering this, gen_python (F-18), and the v0.1 parser that silently skipped unknown lines and thereby parsed a manual into a different world.

title: A ledger client's scorecard close had zero retries, and a lost close means the score never existed
what_happened: arc-recon/client.py:309's close_scorecard is a bare self.request() with no retry, while the same defect (D-015) had already been fixed in baseline-arms/harness/arc_client.py:284 (tries=8) and theoria-arm/harness/arc.py:181 (tries=40). A score exists only in the response to a successful close, so a dropped close silently destroys the measurement.
why_it_was_invisible: PARTNER_SYNC records the consequence as silent by nature: a closed scorecard that cannot be retrieved leaves no error at the call site, only a missing number later.
detected_by: OPS-R harness review, noted as an open hole outside its proposal's scope
detection_latency: unknown; the same fix had already landed in two of three call sites

title: Territory self-audits repeatedly waved through defects that a second reader found immediately
what_happened: A recurring shape across the day rather than one event, and each instance is a commit whose title is its own admission. C1's world factory shipped with 'a QC that missed its own bar'. battery v2.1 pre-registered four defences, of which 'two did not work as predicted'. worldgen's variant-pair work found 'nine things my own tests waved through'. C8's handover manual, given to two fresh readers, produced 53 items with zero wrong answers -- and seven defects found on the way; a further pass found the manual had 'lied to them' in two ways. P5's release kit found the first thing its own reproduce script caught was 'a bug I shipped', and a stranger's run then exposed seven documentation defects and a set of code defects.
why_it_was_invisible: A territory's own suite is written by the same context that wrote the code, so it encodes the same assumptions. The repo's pattern is that the defect count on first external contact is consistently high and consistently surprising to the author -- which is the strongest argument in the corpus for adversarial review as a standing practice rather than a milestone.
detected_by: second readers, adversarial reviews and handover tests, in every case
fix: No single fix. The practice that caught them -- fresh-reader handover tests, adversarial review passes, and a reproduce script run from a clean checkout -- was adopted repeatedly and is the corpus's most reliable detector.

title: The reflex layer held its lock for 34 minutes and every subsequent tick returned early without writing a log line
what_happened: One reflex run stalled while holding the lock. Each five-minute invocation thereafter hit `if time.time() - os.path.getmtime(LOCK) < 1500: return 0` and exited silently -- roughly seven consecutive no-ops. schtasks reported Running, Last Result 0, and the last log line was a perfectly normal MERGED.
