Separately, run()'s default timeout of 2400s exceeds the lock staleness threshold of 1500s, so two runs can legally overlap: the two numbers are the wrong way round.
why_it_was_invisible: OPS-M's line: 'only the mtime was wrong, and nothing watches mtime.' Every status-shaped signal agreed the automation was healthy, and the early return is a designed, silent path -- a skipped cycle and a quiet cycle produce identical output, which is none.
detected_by: OPS-M cycle 6
fix: Reported; the standing recommendation is that a stall must write a line, and that lock staleness must exceed the run timeout rather than the reverse.

title: The probe added after the reflex outage checked whether the task was enabled, not whether it worked -- and the next failure landed exactly in its blind spot
what_happened: After the reflex layer's death, a scheduled_tasks probe was added. The very next failure mode was 'enabled, triggering on schedule, crashing on every run', which that probe reports green. OPS-M's formulation: 启用与运行是两件事 -- being enabled and running are two different things.
why_it_was_invisible: The probe was built from the previous incident's symptom rather than its mechanism. State is cheap to read and effect is not, so the probe read state. It is the third occurrence of this shape in the same subsystem.
detected_by: OPS-M, cycle following the outage
fix: Proposed a clock rather than a judgement: reflex.log mtime older than 15 minutes is red. Escalated to a fleet-wide rule -- 探针必须验证效果，不能只验证状态 (a probe must verify effect, not merely state).

title: pid_alive(0) returns True, so the revival mechanism was quietly off for every task-dispatched agent
what_happened: dispatch.py:312 writes "pid": 0 for entries dispatched via scheduled task. pid_alive(0) evaluates to True on this platform, so all 20 via-task registry entries read reaped: null while all 20 scheduled tasks no longer existed, and exits.json contains zero W- exits. The same criterion is hand-copied into three further places (dispatch.py:130, quota.py:96, scan.py:933) plus the revival gate at reflex.py:159.
why_it_was_invisible: A liveness predicate that always answers yes produces a fleet that always looks alive. Nothing cross-checked the registry against the task table, and the duplicated criterion means a correction in one place leaves three copies wrong.
detected_by: OPS-R harness review
fix: Reported with the duplication called out as the deeper problem; the criterion belongs in one place.

title: The quota detector's signature table had no entry for "session limit", so a real death was missed by both detection paths
what_happened: monitor/dispatch-logs/S3-spend-gate-20260728T035910Z.log:3 reads 'You've hit your session limit - resets 3:20pm (Asia/Shanghai)'. quota.py:38-42's phrase table does not contain it. Combined with F-63, the same log was missed by both detection lines and quota_state.json stayed mode: normal. The session that died was the monitor's own top-priority dispatch, S3-spend-gate.
why_it_was_invisible: A phrase table is a closed enumeration of an open set. An unmatched message is not an error -- it is simply no detection, which renders as a healthy fleet. The highest-priority item dying is exactly the case a healthy-looking fleet hides.
detected_by: OPS-R harness review
fix: Reported. The structural point is the same as F-10 and F-26: a hand-maintained list asserting something about the world, with nothing checking it against the world.

title: The exam grader read unparseable answers as the substantive claim "never", so a blank answer sheet scored full marks on the hardest question
what_happened: V4's self-test of the grader found that answers it could not parse were coerced to the value `never`, which happens to be the true answer for the 'imperceptible at this level' variant. A completely blank submission therefore scored 1.600/144 with full marks on the hardest item. A second defect: every scoring band is Band(0.0, x) -- bounded above, open below -- so a grader that quietly under-scores cannot be detected by the bands.
why_it_was_invisible: A parse failure that produces a default value rather than an error is indistinguishable from a genuine answer, and the default happened to coincide with a correct answer. The grader is the instrument that judges everything else, and it was the instrument nobody had graded.
detected_by: RES-1 running V4-exam-selftest -- the self-check caught a defect already live in production on its first round
detection_latency: unknown; caught on the first self-test
fix: Recorded as D-EX-014 and D-EX-013 and fixed. Related and separately found: the marker had only ever been tested at its endpoints, leaving a hole in the middle of its range.

title: The spend gate was never wired to the arm's main cost axis, so $6.32 of model spend never entered the shared pool
what_happened: A3-campaign-devpile's red line requires spend to pass through spend_gate.reserve(). A grep across the whole arm found zero imports of the gate. ARC actions are counted server-side by env_proxy, but desk model calls shell out directly to `claude -p` and bypass the gate entirely -- so the single real g50t run's $6.32 never entered the pool, constrained only by an in-arm cost_ceiling_usd.
why_it_was_invisible: RES-1's phrasing: 红线目前是一条未实现的要求，不是一个已存在的控制 -- the red line is presently an unimplemented requirement, not an existing control. The pool reports a number; a bypassed writer makes that number small rather than absent, which reads as thrift rather than blindness.
detected_by: RES-1, on claiming the campaign item and checking its own preconditions before spending
detection_latency: unknown -- found before further spend, not after

title: The terms canary's word counts moved because the instrument changed scale, not because the page changed
what_happened: The terms canary's first normalised word counts (35124 / 20806) looked like page drift on an externally-owned policy page. The pages had not changed; the canary's own normalisation had. OPS-B's line: 量具变了，不是被测物变了 ... 探针也会说谎，当它换了刻度而没人记得的时候 -- the gauge changed, not the thing measured; a probe lies too, when it changes its scale and nobody remembers.
why_it_was_invisible: A canary reports a delta. A delta cannot distinguish a change in the subject from a change in the measure unless the measure is versioned, which it was not. This is the alarming-direction twin of F-52.
detected_by: OPS-B cycle 4, which titled its own commit '顺便逮到一个自己造的假信号' -- incidentally caught a false signal of my own making
fix: The normalisation was pinned so the baseline and the reading are on the same scale. Companion near-miss the same day: Bash stdout renders GBK on this host, so valid UTF-8 bus files display as mojibake, and OPS-A nearly filed a 'bus messages corrupted' drift report before checking the bytes.

title: A second session swept another agent's staged files onto master, because the first fix for this had been scoped to one directory
what_happened: After F-31, commit a24e899 -- authored under a different track and titled for A4a's PARTNER_SYNC entry -- swallowed all four of OPS-M's staged files. The 12:40Z remedy for the first incident had been scoped to the monitor's own committing behaviour, and this actor was a different session entirely.
why_it_was_invisible: Git staging is a per-worktree global. Any session committing at the repo root with -A or . captures every other session's staged work, and the capture is invisible at commit time because the diff looks like ordinary progress. The first incident's fix addressed the actor rather than the shared resource -- the exact failure the repo's own rule ('invariants hang on the resource, not on the writer') names.
detected_by: OPS-M, finding its staged files already on master for the second time that day
fix: Escalated for the rule to be put in ALL.md and CHARTER.md as a fleet-wide requirement rather than one session's discipline. A bus note on the repeat sweep was filed at d751ccd.

title: The fleet broadcast file had one status field, four readers, and no per-reader acknowledgement
what_happened: monitor/mailbox/ALL.md is read by four ops sessions and carries a single `status:` slot. OPS-M refused to write it -- ALL.md 的 status 我不改 -- because one agent's acknowledgement would mask the other three's unread state, asked for a non-overwriting convention at 06:16Z, received no answer, and asked again at 11:18Z. OPS-A, OPS-B and RES-2 independently made the same choice and replied in their own mailboxes instead.
why_it_was_invisible: It did not fail -- four agents independently recognised the hazard and refused to use the field, which is why nothing broke. The failure is latent and structural: a mutable single-slot status with N writers and no protocol, whose safety depended entirely on every participant declining to use it.
detected_by: OPS-M, refusing rather than writing; corroborated by three other sessions making the same call independently
fix: Superseded by the per-agent message bus (monitor/bus/<agent>/in.jsonl + cursor.json + out.jsonl), which gives every reader its own cursor and its own ack channel.

title: A new session inherited its predecessor's bus cursor and silently skipped three unread orders, one of which was a $200 budget authorisation
what_happened: When RES-1 changed sessions, the new session resumed the bus cursor at its predecessor's last_seq. Three orders the predecessor had never read were already below that mark and were therefore skipped in silence -- items 2, 3 and 5, the last being the campaign's $200 budget authorisation. It was recovered only because the monitor noticed three missing acks and re-sent the contents as an urgent message at seq 6.
why_it_was_invisible: The cursor records position, not comprehension. Advancing it is the same operation whether a message was read or merely passed over, and a skipped order produces no ack -- an absence, which only shows up if somebody is counting acks. HOSTED.md's protocol claims 换一个会话不丢任何东西 (changing session loses nothing); this is the gap in that claim.
detected_by: the monitor, by counting missing acks
fix: Recovered ad hoc by re-sending. The monitor put the general question to OPS-R rather than assuming it had found the only instance: 还有哪些状态在换会话时会被静默继承或丢失 -- what other state is silently inherited or lost at session change?

title: The bus was declared the fleet's only channel while four of six mailboxes had never read it
what_happened: OPS-M observed that of six bus mailboxes only OPS-B and OPS-M had a cursor.json -- OPS-A, OPS-R, RES-1 and RES-2 had never read the bus at all. The state persists in the tree now: monitor/bus/OPS-R/ holds the single largest order (seq 2, the five-silent-failures retrospective) with no cursor.json and no out.jsonl, so there is no evidence it was ever read or acknowledged; monitor/bus/RES-3/ has only out.jsonl and can speak but has no inbound channel.
why_it_was_invisible: This is the substrate under F-03: the probe that should have reported 'four sessions have never read' was itself mis-decoding and reporting 'all acknowledged'. A channel declared authoritative before its readers are attached looks identical to a channel working perfectly.
detected_by: OPS-M, incidentally, while reporting on something else
fix: The probe was fixed (F-03). The unread mailboxes are still unread as of this capture.

title: An agent died inside a one-hour sleep and nobody noticed for two and a half hours; its staleness threshold gave fifteen hours of cover
what_happened: OPS-A's predecessor died inside a background sleep with no completion record. monitor/audit/HEARTBEAT stopped at 03:36Z cycle=1; the 04:36 and 05:36 cycles produced nothing; a human restarted it at 06:15. OPS-R noted the same trap applied to itself: scan.py grants OPS-R a 900-minute staleness threshold against a 720-minute contract cycle, so 我若死在睡眠里，你会晚 15 小时才看见 -- if I die in my sleep, you will see it fifteen hours late.
why_it_was_invisible: Sleeping and dead are the same observable. The staleness threshold, set generously so as not to produce false alarms, is precisely the size of the blind spot; setting it above the contract period guarantees at least one full missed cycle is undetectable.
detected_by: a human noticing the audit had stopped; the threshold arithmetic was then self-reported by OPS-R
detection_latency: ~2h30m for the death; the threshold gap was found by inspection
fix: Requested: a scheduled task re-pasting the boot phrase, on the stated grounds of 不再假装休眠是可靠的 -- no longer pretending sleep is reliable.

title: An agent slept twelve hours on a contract rhythm that had been superseded six hours earlier
what_happened: A hot-reconfiguration changed the ops contract cycle from twelve hours to four. One agent had already entered a twelve-hour sleep under the old rhythm and woke into a fleet that had changed around it. The monitor's note: 你上一轮睡了 12 小时 -- 那是旧节律，契约已改为 4 小时一轮.
why_it_was_invisible: The 'edit one file and the whole fleet complies next cycle' mechanism has no effect on an agent that is inside a long sleep, and there is no signal distinguishing 'complying with the current contract' from 'complying with a contract that no longer exists'.
detected_by: the monitor, on the agent's next wake
fix: Handled by telling the agent on wake. No mechanism prevents recurrence.

title: Three consecutive context-wall handoffs in one lane, each losing the run's opening -- and the artifact that survived them was a plan written to disk
what_happened: RES-2 hit the context wall after P8, again after P9-figures, and again during P5 planning, where 枚举器一行没写 (not one line of the enumerator was written). RES-1 stopped mid-A4a and left an explicit anti-re-claim instruction, because the board still showing A4a locked to RES-1 was deliberate: this is a continuation, not a re-claim, so do not run board.py claim again.
why_it_was_invisible: Not invisible so much as unbudgeted: the cost of a handoff is a whole session opening, paid every time, and nothing in the dispatch accounting represented it. The mitigation that worked is recorded plainly -- BUILD_PLAN.md was 让这件活能跨上下文活下来的那件产物 (the artifact that lets this work survive across contexts).
detected_by: self-reported by both standing researchers
fix: No mechanism, but a practice that demonstrably works and matches CLAUDE.md's standing instruction: write the plan and the run state to disk as you go -- a session's context evaporates, the disk is the memory.

title: A priority-1 item vanished from the board entirely because territory mutex filtered it out of both lists
what_happened: A3-campaign-devpile (priority 1, lane campaign) could not be claimed because its territory theoria-arm was held by E3-engines-online. Territory mutex removed it from `available`, and `blocked` counts only dependency blocks, so 从板面上看它像凭空消失了 -- from the board it looked as though it had vanished into thin air. The item is the paper's largest weight gap: WP3, 20% of the weight, 30% complete.
why_it_was_invisible: The board has two visible buckets and three states. An item excluded from both lists is not reported anywhere, and a shorter available list reads as a busy fleet. The highest-priority item is exactly the one whose disappearance costs most.
detected_by: RES-1, on going looking for the campaign item and not finding it
fix: Reported; the board needs a third bucket for territory-blocked items.

title: Two figure pipelines by two authors who never compared results, and the paper printed a count that was wrong
what_happened: papers/phase1-workshop/figures/ and the root figures/ both produce three of the same figures, 由两个从未比对过的作者各算一遍 -- computed twice by two authors who never compared. A parity check found 12 agreements, 1 one-sided, and 1 real disagreement: the paper reported 18 verdicts where the true number is 17. The extra came from P-03, for which the log never wrote a verdict, and the paper's parser counted a 'see body' placeholder string as one.
why_it_was_invisible: Two independent pipelines agreeing is evidence; two independent pipelines never compared is not. Nothing forced the comparison, and a plausible-looking integer in a paper has no error signal. Related: a third instance of duplicate effort had ablation-arm/verify.sh written twice by two sessions, with the monitor conceding its own version was worse and discarding it.
detected_by: RES-2, by building a parity checker between the two pipelines
fix: Section 3.1 corrected to 17. Figures were subsequently sourced from the pipeline, with the second figure made the witness.

title: Merging was blocked for 96 minutes by a budget it is structurally incapable of spending
what_happened: reflex.py:184's `if not hold:` disabled the ci_merge step entirely. But `hold` tracks Claude's session quota, while ci_merge.py is git plus pytest with zero API calls -- grep-verified. 合并被一个它根本花不掉的预算挡住了 -- merging was blocked by a budget it cannot spend.
why_it_was_invisible: A blocked queue with an explained cause looks like correct backpressure. OPS-M's structural reading is the useful part: this is the same coupling in its third form -- merge first shared a process with the reviver, then a scheduled task, now a single boolean. 要拆开的不只是进程，是判断 -- what needs separating is not just the process but the judgement.
detected_by: OPS-M cycle 4
fix: Decoupled, with the comment stating the reason in the code: 'runs even under quota hold: it spends zero tokens'. Verified by effect rather than by reading -- merge.log shows four branches auto-merged between 11:42Z and 11:48Z while quota_state.mode was continuously hold.

title: The fleet contract required an agent to fan out to subagents that its own harness forbids it from calling
what_happened: Two clauses were added to OPS-A's contract: mandatory parallel subagents, and a mandatory adversarial subagent to refute any conclusive output. OPS-A reported that it physically cannot execute them -- 我这个会话的 harness 有一条硬约束：未经用户明确要求不得调用 Agent/subagent 工具，而它的优先级高于仓库里的契约文件 (this session's harness carries a hard constraint against calling subagent tools without explicit user request, and it outranks the repository's contract files). Its conclusion: 不要把我的产出按已经过对抗复核来计 -- do not count my output as having been adversarially reviewed.
why_it_was_invisible: A contract file can be hot-loaded onto an agent whose harness silently outranks it. Compliance is unobservable from outside: an agent that cannot fan out and an agent that chose not to produce identical artifacts. Only voluntary self-report revealed the gap -- and the gap matters because downstream consumers were about to treat that output as adversarially reviewed when it was not.
detected_by: the agent itself, self-reporting a capability it lacked
detection_latency: one cycle from the clause landing
fix: Not mechanised. The disclosure was accepted and the review status of that agent's output downgraded accordingly.

title: A contamination path that produces no API call, no ledger entry, and therefore nothing any audit can see
what_happened: OPS-B established by live test -- clean session, no login, no key, no cookies -- that arcprize.org/scorecards/<uuid> renders without redirecting to /login, so per-frame replay of any game is publicly viewable without authentication. The consequence is load-bearing: 这条路径不产生 API 调用、不进任何账本，contamination.py 审的是 every call ever made，所以点开一局封存 replay 时审计一片绿而污染已发生 -- this path produces no API call and enters no ledger, and contamination.py audits every call ever made, so opening a sealed game's replay leaves the audit entirely green while the contamination has occurred. The policy page itself carries a link to sealed game re86's replay, recorded and not clicked.
why_it_was_invisible: The audit's subject is API traffic and this path generates none. It is not a gap in the check but a mismatch between the check's domain and the risk's domain. OPS-B deliberately declined to build a probe: the only auditable trace would be browser history, which is surveillance of a person.
detected_by: OPS-B, by live test in a clean session
fix: No probe is possible; a red line in prose was drafted instead (browser-ops/REDLINE-replay-proposed-text.md). This is the corpus's clearest case of a risk that must be held by discipline because it cannot be held by instrumentation -- and it should be read alongside F-08, where instrumentation existed and was simply not wired up.

title: The permissive half of a two-part proposal landed and the containment half did not, leaving the loosening standing alone
what_happened: arc-recon adopted the permissive half of OPS-B's terms proposal at 0a71c1c -- the ACCESS_CHECK item was reopened and closed as less restrictive -- while the containment half did not follow. The now-standalone sentence 'caching ARC data locally is permitted, and no permission needs to be sought for it' sits with nothing saying what the cache contains, while enabling local mode by default pulls all 25 games' source code into environment_files/ and the official runner's --game default plays all available games. A whole-repo grep finds environment_files in exactly one place, as a permission argument. OPS-B reported the identical structural gap a second time for the CLAUDE.md / piles.json half of a later proposal: 两条是同一类东西，却只有一条有归宿 -- these are the same kind of thing, and only one of them has a home.
why_it_was_invisible: A proposal is adopted clause by clause by whoever owns each destination file. The permissive clause has an obvious owner and lands; the containment clause often has no owner, and its absence produces no signal. The net effect of partial adoption is monotonically toward loosening.
detected_by: OPS-B cycle 2, tracking its own proposals against the tree
fix: Escalated for adjudication. D-1 was upgraded from argument to live measurement. The structural gap -- ops-session output having no destination in the plan -- is the same one recorded as F-45.

title: A component that needs one administrator action was reported three cycles running with no path to force it in front of the human
what_happened: TheoriaServe is absent from schtasks entirely -- never registered, not merely disabled. Registration was refused by permissions and requires the user to run it once as administrator. OPS-M reported it at 08:17Z, at 09:40Z, and again at 12:55Z: 卡两轮了，这条建议尽快转给用户 (stuck for two cycles, please pass this to the user soon). A parallel case: the .env API key cannot be revoked or rotated because the account panel's only key (a4***a91b) is not the repo's key (71***05dd) under the same masking, so nobody knows which account owns the live credential.
why_it_was_invisible: The fleet's escalation channel is the monitor's inbox, and the monitor cannot perform an administrator action either. An item that no amount of autonomy can clear accumulates in a queue designed for items that autonomy clears, where it is indistinguishable from work in progress.
detected_by: OPS-M and OPS-B respectively, both re-reporting across cycles
detection_latency: 3 cycles for TheoriaServe; the key ownership question is still open
fix: The board gained a needs_human designation, used correctly for the release-licence letter -- the R2 item states plainly that applying for permission is a human's decision and must not be done by an agent, and the auditor retracted its own earlier advice to the contrary. A general escalation path for administrator-blocked items did not land.

title: One observation produced three successive diagnoses, and only the third named a defect anyone could fix -- our own
what_happened: INC-001 and INC-002 declared the live-API programme blocked: 400 game-not-found on three of four dev games, and 4/48 RESETs plus 0/8 ACTIONs succeeding across four request-body shapes. Both were reversed. INC-001b/002a replaced them with a server-side wave model. INC-007a then superseded that too, proving by interleaved A/B (arms on different games, both orderings) that the client kept no cookie jar: the cookie-carrying arm got 20/20 first-attempt RESETs, the cookie-less arm 0/20, and the same twenty commands cost 190 HTTP calls before the fix and 20 after -- 9.5x -- with frame hashes byte-identical across the change. The chain runs entitlement, then backend waves, then our own missing cookie jar.
why_it_was_invisible: Every diagnosis fit the evidence available to it, and each was more specific than the last. The failure mode is a blocking verdict on a shared resource being treated as terminal: work stops, so no further evidence arrives that could overturn it.
detected_by: cross-track -- baseline-arms found it first. Its pilots drove 13-15 successful actions per game and its D-005 reclassified the 400 as transient at a measured 5.07 HTTP per successful action, reported on PARTNER_SYNC before arc-recon re-ran. INC-001b's own detail field credits it.
detection_latency: ~2h30m to the first reversal; the final diagnosis landed the following day
fix: The retry envelope was widened and the cookie jar added, with the handler ordering pinned by a test (HTTPCookieProcessor at 500 runs before HTTPErrorProcessor at 1000, so the jar learns routing cookies from the first 400) -- because if that ordering ever changed the fix would degrade silently with nothing failing. The taxonomy consequence worth carrying: the ledger is append-only, so reversals arrive as new records carrying supersedes_diagnosis_in while INC-001, INC-001a and INC-002 remain on disk still stamped severity: blocking. Anyone counting severities off the raw file over-reports blocking incidents roughly threefold. Standing lesson: one track's blocking verdict on a shared resource should not be terminal until a second track has failed to reproduce it.

title: A short game id returned HTTP 200 with a counterfeit frame, and sixteen of twenty actions were spent on it
what_happened: Recorded as INC-005 and cross-registered as INC-BA-002. Acting on another track's status-code-only finding that short ids work, the corrected precheck run alternated short ids into ACTION retries. Short-id 200s are counterfeit: six of six on g50t returned the pristine initial frame 801726dc499f3f52 with n_frames=1 and levels_completed=0 regardless of real session progress, and in baseline-arms' probe log the nonexistent ACTION7 also returned 200 under a short id. This produced a false 'FAIL, first divergence at step 3' verdict and burned 16 of g50t's 20-action budget, which is why g50t's PASS is 3/3 rather than 9/9.
why_it_was_invisible: A 200 is the strongest available success signal and it was lying. The originating finding, INC-BA-002, was explicitly status-code-only; the lesson both tracks recorded verbatim is that a status code is not evidence, content is. Compare INC-BA-002's earlier sibling: the permission wall where exit 0 was read as success (F-16).
detected_by: arc-recon, cross-track -- the track that made the original claim did not find it
detection_latency: unknown; caught after the budget was spent
fix: Full ids enforced on every attempt, with the short-to-full map in precheck.json's id_map, and short ids banned from all future harness request bodies. The pilot data was uncontaminated because those harnesses always used full ids. Recurred in another track: proxy's sealed-pile guard was completely blind to the short id ls20 until its red team found it.

title: The redactor leaked session tokens into a tracked, publishable ledger -- and the values are still in pushed git history
what_happened: Recorded as INC-008. A stickiness probe wrote raw Set-Cookie headers -- including GAMESESSION, a bearer token for a live game session -- verbatim into data/recon_ledger.jsonl, which is tracked and which Theoria's Phase 4 publishes. 55 calls were affected. The mechanism: redaction discipline lived inside client._record, and the probe wrote its own ledger writer because it needed response headers that _record does not capture. 'A rule enforced in one function holds only for callers of that function.'
why_it_was_invisible: The redactor was working correctly for every caller that used it. A second writer bypassing it produces perfectly well-formed ledger rows; nothing at the file level asserted that no row may contain a cookie value.
detected_by: self, while writing the cookie-jar fix -- i.e. found by the session that was congratulating itself for a different catch
fix: Fixed forward and backward: names-only logging; a redact_ledger.py that replaced the 55 values at byte level so untouched entries stay byte-identical and the diff is exactly 55 lines; and a test asserting no ledger entry carries a cookie value, watched failing on all 55 first. NOT fixed: the values remain in git history at commit 29c631e, which is pushed. Removing them means rewriting a published branch, and that is explicitly left as the owner's decision. Exposure is bounded to abandoned development-pile sessions and the API key was never involved.

title: A failed request left no ledger row, so the audit underpinning the project's most load-bearing claim had a hole in it
what_happened: Found in INC-009's five-lens adversarial review of the cookie patch, run before the after-run's actions were spent: 30 findings raised, 17 survived independent refutation. request() caught only HTTPError, so a timeout carrying a sealed game_id would leave no ledger row at all -- invisible to contamination.py's sealed-pile audit and invisible to the test asserting that audit is clean. Three companion defects in the same review: the redactor could leak through itself (cookie_names() split Set-Cookie on ',' and could emit a fragment of a value as if it were a name); the cookie record was in the wrong tense; and the value-detector test could not fail, because it flagged a field only if '=' appeared in the text while the name lists it checked are produced by split('=')[0].
why_it_was_invisible: An audit over a ledger can only see what the ledger records. A write path that fails without writing produces a shorter, entirely consistent ledger. The review's own summary is the corpus's most quoted line: 'the instrument you just built to check something is the instrument nobody has checked' -- all three defects were in code written by the session that had just caught INC-008.
detected_by: an adversarial review deliberately scheduled before the expensive run, not after
fix: All fixed; test_hygiene.py grew to 40 tests with 7 regressions, each carrying a negative control. No published number changed; one claim was corrected from 16 expected hashes to the 11 discriminating ones. The pinned jar had also made the retry envelope weaker than what it replaced -- all 40 retries now hitting the same replica -- fixed by dropping AWSALB* every 5 failures while keeping GAMESESSION.

title: A subagent sent to the public web to find citations read nine sealed games' mechanics before it could recognise the page
what_happened: Recorded as INC-BA-001. Theoria.md contains no citations at all -- no arXiv id, no URL, no references section, grep-confirmed -- so locating the upstream Schema artifacts required public web search. It was delegated to a subagent with the sealed-pile constraint stated up front. The subagent obeyed the part it could, relaying no mechanics to its principal, but the project landing page put game content early enough that it had already read several sealed games' mechanics before recognising the page and stopping. Nine games at four depths: ls20 and ft09 material (ls20 is the page's running example with concrete transition rules; ft09 is named with its hidden mechanic), one slightly above minor, five minor, one negligible. API calls to the sealed pile: zero.
why_it_was_invisible: The constraint was given and was followed. Deciding whether a page is safe requires reading it, and the task was to go and find pages. The repo records this as a tension inherent to the task rather than an execution failure, and the F-11 ruling accepts that reading. Structurally it is invisible to instrumentation for the same reason as F-79: no API call, no ledger entry.
detected_by: the subagent itself, self-reporting immediately to its principal
fix: Not fixable -- a read mechanic cannot be unread. Disposition: ls20 and ft09 quarantined, seven retained with mandatory sensitivity analysis, sealed claim set cut from 21 to 19, piles.json untouched and still hashing to 3feca53e...41bbc19a. The structural cost is recorded honestly: ft09 was the only member of sealed_only_families, so quarantining it leaves the claim set with no representative of the one family the development pile never shows -- the exact property the cut existed to preserve. Standing rule added: a subagent sent to the public web can protect its principal's context but not its own, so the cost of such a search near sealed material is one contaminated context and must be priced before dispatch. The whitelist built in response failed closed on first run -- upstream paths carry 4-char prefixes while the whitelist tested full ids, so all 165 files were denied and zero bytes fetched, and the subagent stopped and reported rather than loosening the list.

title: Four offline proof runs, 44 tests and two mock dry runs missed both live faults, because the rehearsal used a different model from the flight
what_happened: Recorded as INC-TA-004: two live runs aborted on arm defects costing 11 actions and $2.05. Attempt 1 -- the manual declared landmarks the level generator never places, ProblemError on every compile, 5 actions and $1.31. Attempt 2 -- the desk had tools and used them: `claude -p --max-turns 1` returned stop_reason: tool_use because the model tried `mkdir && cat >` to write its answer to a file rather than print it, consuming the only turn on one tool call: 6 actions, $0.73, 251s, and 19,957 output tokens nobody could read.
why_it_was_invisible: Offline worlds are small enough that a manual never needs a landmark, so fault 1 could not arise in rehearsal. And the offline desk ran claude-haiku-4-5 while the live run used claude-opus-5 -- haiku answered in text where opus reached for a file. Neither fault is world behaviour; both are arm behaviour that only the flight configuration exhibits.
detected_by: the arm itself, on live contact
detection_latency: immediate, but only after real money was spent
fix: Fixed with --tools "" plus --max-turns 2, verified for $0.0149 on haiku before spending another action. Both aborts archived in full as runs/*-aborted/ABORTED.md rather than deleted. The stated lesson is the generalisable one: rehearse with the model you will fly with, or accept that the rehearsal did not cover the model.

title: An upstream schema change ate a paid model call in silence -- the provider was billed $2.69 and the ledger recorded nothing
what_happened: Recorded as INC-TA-006. desk.calls read 1 and cli_cost_usd read $2.694961, so the provider had been paid, while desk_log.json was [] and the ledger held zero model_call records. The arm's `except Exception` recorded 'the desk failed' and went back for more evidence, so it would have kept paying $2.70 per call producing nothing until the cost ceiling stopped it. Root cause: LEDGER_FORMAT.md section 4 closed the model_call field set after P-8 landed, invalidating five fields P-8 wrote (beat, label, proxied, proxy_gap, transport). The arm imports proxy/ as a library, so the change arrived on a commit this track never touched and was never announced.
why_it_was_invisible: Tests check hand-built dictionaries, so the gap was not a missing assertion but a missing subject. And the upstream pin missed it because nothing compares pins between runs -- the incident's own line: 'a pin that is written and never diffed does not prevent an incident; it documents one, afterwards, for someone who already knows to look.'
detected_by: the arm, on reconciling its own cost figures against its own ledger
fix: Fixed within the arm. The general gap -- a written pin that nothing diffs -- was escalated and is the reason the incident is worth keeping: it is a shared-library dependency across tracks that communicate only through git history.

title: A cost table under-billed by 6.8%, and the error was only visible because the run recorded two independent cost figures
what_happened: Recorded as INC-TA-003. proxy/cost.py reads the flat usage.cache_creation_input_tokens key, which does not say which cache TTL was purchased; the TTL is reported, in the nested usage.cache_creation object, which cost.py does not read. Measured on the first live theorize call, where all 20,736 cache-creation tokens were 1-hour writes: the table said $1.218392 against the CLI's own $1.307727, a gap of 6.8%, of which the 1h multiplier explains 87% and a residual 0.9% is left explicitly unexplained rather than rounded away.
why_it_was_invisible: The incident says it plainly: this finding exists only because the run records two cost figures. A cross-check against a single source would have reported the table's number as the answer. And it compounds -- Theoria's whole thesis is about the shape of the bill, with cache reads as the axis it is placed on.
detected_by: the arm, by recording two cost sources and comparing them
fix: Reported, not fixed -- proxy/ belongs to another track. The diagnosis is now computed automatically for every run by armtools/archive.py::_cache_ttl_diagnosis so it appears in every MANIFEST.json and, in the incident's phrase, 'cannot quietly stop being true'.

title: A structural zero was about to be read as a measured small number on the paper's decisive axis
what_happened: Recorded as INC-TA-005. The arm's cache_read_input_tokens is exactly 0 against 61,214 cache-creation tokens, because every `claude -p` is a fresh process in a fresh temp directory -- deliberate, it is the seal that keeps the desk from reading Theoria.md, the pile cut and other arms' traces. So each call creates a cache it will never read. This matters because Theoria.md's central wager is a table whose distinguishing column is cache reads per game (Schema ~1e8, Theoria predicted ~1e6, bare CC ~6e5). The arm cannot report a number in that column: its zero is a different quantity, not a small one.
why_it_was_invisible: A zero in a numeric column is indistinguishable from a measured zero. Nothing in the ledger format marks a value as structurally unavailable versus measured-as-none, and a Phase 2 battery re-pricing every arm's history from one ledger would read this zero as genuine.
detected_by: the arm, self-reporting a measurement hazard rather than publishing the number
fix: Recorded as a standing Phase 2 measurement hazard; the arm reports total input tokens re-sent per turn instead (~20,000 per call, three calls, no growth). Same family as the repo's other framing catch: the timeline had claimed that zero surprises implied zero calls.

title: An inference was carried as a measurement for three days, in two documents, on the strength of a syllogism in the design file
what_happened: Recorded as INC-AR-010. 'The environment has an internal tick' reached both ACCESS_CHECK.md and README.md as a settled access-check answer. It was never measured -- the measurement was 'frame is a list', and the tick was an inference from that. It survived because Theoria.md:299 names animation and internal tick as two candidate causes of the same observation while :301 compresses them into a syllogism, which was then quoted as though it were the finding.
why_it_was_invisible: An inference and a measurement look identical once written into a findings document; nothing distinguishes 'observed' from 'concluded' in the prose. No wrong artifact shipped only because every consumer had independently been taking frames[-1] for convenience.
detected_by: W-1250, while closing the item, by reading the two Theoria.md lines against each other
fix: Corrected. Note for anyone auditing this taxonomy: INC-AR-010 and INC-AR-011 are recorded in arc-recon/data/incidents.jsonl only on branches (97c1cbd, a16eab9), not in the master copy of that file, while monitor/inbox/20260728T151000Z-...md:71 cites INC-AR-011 as if it were there -- a dangling citation, and an instance of F-92.

title: The sole evidence for a Phase 1 gate item existed only as untracked files inside a worktree, one prune away from deletion
what_happened: Recorded as INC-AR-011. P-20's per-frame probe data -- the only evidence for a Phase 1 gate item -- existed as an untracked directory inside .worktrees/wt-p20/ with no MANIFEST and no RUN_STATE; a git worktree prune would have deleted it. It then compounded: W-5200 salvaged the data and wrote the adjudication, and was killed, probably by the 09:35Z session-limit hold, with all of it still uncommitted, where it sat five hours.
why_it_was_invisible: Same mechanism as F-47: every fleet instrument reads git, so uncommitted work is indistinguishable from no work. The standing lesson recorded is the sharpest phrasing of it in the corpus -- 'the disk is only the memory if the disk is a branch' -- which is a direct amendment to CLAUDE.md's 'the disk is the memory'.
fix: Salvaged. Residual explicitly recorded as unfixed: nothing sweeps worktrees for uncommitted work whose owner is gone.

title: A test appended two rows to another track's real, tracked, append-only ledger, because a default argument had bound at definition time
what_happened: Recorded inside INC-010. The first version of new tests tried to monkeypatch ledger.PROBE_PATH, which does not work because the default binds at function-definition time -- so two test entries were appended to baseline-arms' real, tracked, append-only probe_log.jsonl.
why_it_was_invisible: Monkeypatching a module attribute that a default argument already captured produces no error at all: the patch succeeds, the function ignores it, and the write lands in the real file. Append-only files have no signal for two extra rows.
detected_by: self, immediately
fix: Reverted with git checkout, restoring the file to its committed 1945 lines; the tests now replace ledger.probe outright, and a further test asserts the file's size does not move. The surrounding cross-track edit was deliberately done in a worktree rather than the main checkout precisely because two of the other track's processes were live -- 'INC-BA-003 is precisely the incident about two sessions colliding in that directory' -- and the merge hazard was flagged on PARTNER_SYNC rather than left to be found at merge.

title: ci_merge's trailing git pull runs in the merge referee's own working tree and swapped files out from under a live measurement
what_happened: ci_merge.main() ends with a git pull whose cwd is the repo root -- which is also OPS-M's working tree. Mid-measurement it changed the tree underneath the measurement: 本轮我先数到 14 个目录、再数到 15 个 (this cycle I counted 14 directories, then 15).
why_it_was_invisible: Both numbers are correct for their instant. A count taken before and used after is silently stale, and there is no error -- only a quietly inconsistent report.
detected_by: OPS-M, on getting two different counts in one cycle
fix: Classed as a measurement hazard rather than a defect; the mitigation adopted is to enumerate at measurement time rather than reuse a count.

title: figures/verify.sh is red on master right now, with five source hashes drifted, and the item that depends on it is still on the board
what_happened: A by-product of the RES-3 negative-control census: figures/verify.sh fails on master because SOURCES.sha256 has five drifted sources -- THEORIZE_LOG.md's E-08 came from C9, and three cold-start-a2 artifacts came from the ablation arm. The figures are older than their inputs, and P12 depends on them.
why_it_was_invisible: A hash manifest over inputs owned by other territories drifts whenever those territories deliver. Nothing routes that drift back to the figure owner, so a red gate sits red in a territory nobody is currently occupying -- the mirror image of F-41, where a permanently red probe trains people to ignore the cell.
detected_by: RES-3's V11 census, reported rather than fixed because figures was not its territory

title: A tier rename broke a downstream string literal, and one arm had already been red before anyone looked
what_happened: A model-tier rename propagated through configuration but not through a downstream literal comparison, and a0-spike was found already red when the check was made.
why_it_was_invisible: A string literal comparison against a renamed value does not raise -- it simply stops matching, and a stopped match usually routes to a default branch. The arm had been red for some time before anyone happened to run it.
detected_by: OPS-M, during a routine cycle
fix: The literal was corrected. Same family as F-64: a hand-written string asserting a fact about a system that moved.
